AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This and the next block contains all five leveltunes crammed together         in one single block. Notice (3) in the block which is a conversion of         the music 'The Loco-Motion' - I thought it would be a nice touch to         such a train game. However, SilverRock thought they might get in         trouble if I converted it, so... (See comment for         /MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Guldkornekspressen_Levels_v4.sid)" (JCH)(#3)  TITLE: The Loco-Motion ARTIST: Little EvaCOMMENT: Based on the version sung by Kylie Minogue.

TITLE: Guldkornekspressen Levels (v4)
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "(Continued from /MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Guldkornekspressen_Levels_v3.sid)         ...this is how it was changed to make SilverRock happy. As you can         hear, the difference is really not that big. Later on during the         programming of the game, Thomas (the programmer) realized that he         could not fit all the leveltunes into the game, hence this leveltune         was the first to go." (JCH)(#3)  TITLE: The Loco-Motion ARTIST: Little EvaCOMMENT: Based on the version sung by Kylie Minogue.

TITLE: Gunfight
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I managed to code a complete Gunfight game in 1987-1988 - you know,         the stuff with two gunfighters in each side of the screen shooting         each other until one of them enters 'BOOT HILL'. This tune was made in         'Aegis Sonix' - the only tune to be converted using the old method         into Laxity's player." (JCH)

TITLE: Hacktrick
AUTHOR: JCH & The Saint
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "My friend, 'The Saint', hummed the bassline and I made all the rest."         (JCH)

TITLE: Hard On
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The first song done in a player featuring 'Hard restart' - so as you         see, the name is not as naughty as you might think! ;)" (JCH)

TITLE: Hawaii
AUTHOR: JCH & Morten Kristensen (MSK)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A very long tune containing one of the longest solo parts I have ever         done in a C64 tune. The bassline and drums were originally made by         Morten Sigaard Kristensen, but in the end I 'raped' it so much that it         virtually became my own work. The solo part starts at 01:39. Notice         how the tune decays in the end - this was very unusual on the C64."         (JCH)

TITLE: Heavy Hit
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Short, 'end-of-level-monster'-like tune made in a compromise player         which took VERY little rastertime." (JCH)

TITLE: Hexagon Party
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made FOR that party, not AT it. The tune contains quite a lot of         harmonic mistakes, something I often made in that period. These were         often caused by 'lazy' transpositions of the bassline sequence -         instead of creating a new one." (JCH)

TITLE: Hitsong
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Turn It Up [from the movie Who's That Girl] ARTIST: Michael DavidsonCOMMENT: "Converted from a sample on a very old Amiga intro by ECA." (JCH)

TITLE: Hollywood
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A sad, film-like tune." (JCH)

TITLE: Hoppin'
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "An excerpt from 'Sampler #1' - a very fast introtune." (JCH)

TITLE: Horizon Copy-Party
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made at the Horizon copy-party in Sweden." (JCH)

TITLE: Hurricane
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Experimental tune testing the speed changing abilities of the new         player v18. The change happens at 00:15." (JCH)

TITLE: Illegal Man
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "After the music group '20CC' had been in the demo scene for some         time, a sourcecode was hacked and spread on the american BBS. I         managed to get a version of this sourcecode - and tried to fiddle with         it. This is what came out of it. It was composed in assembler and         changes after 15 seconds." (JCH)

TITLE: Imagination
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The second tune made in the NewPlayer v00 series, no effects in the         player." (JCH)

TITLE: Introzak
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Very short introtune made for an intro by 'Channel 42'." (JCH)

TITLE: James Bond Theme
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: James Bond Theme [from the James Bond series of movies] ARTIST: Monty NormanCOMMENT: "Conversion of a 007 theme found on a CD containing James Bond         synthesizer conversions." (JCH)

TITLE: JCH in Visage's Editor
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: Made in 1991, released in 2018.

TITLE: Jewels
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Wouldn't It Be Good [from Human Racing] ARTIST: Nik KershawCOMMENT: "Conversion of an old Nik Kershaw song. The first version of the old         player to feature slide. Many of the tunes in this period didn't use         any slide at all." (JCH)

TITLE: Kinetic
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Kinetic [from the Amiga MOD module] ARTIST: Stefan Jaworski (Nightlight of Kefrens)

TITLE: Knackdick
AUTHOR: JCH & Thomas Mogensen (DRAX)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The only real cooperation tune released by DRAX and I. I must admit         however, that DRAX made about 85% of the tune." (JCH)

TITLE: Labyrint
AUTHOR: JCH & Thomas Mogensen (DRAX)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Labyrinth [from the Amiga game] ARTIST: N.J. Luuring Jr.COMMENT: "A television quiz program which was made popular by a great Danish         former disc-jockey Kim Schumacher was converted by a small Danish firm         as a C64 game. The music was composed on the Amiga by an unknown guy.         'DRAX' was asked to convert the tune for a certain sum of money but,         as he said himself, he wasn't sure he could convert it so he asked me         for help. I completed the conversion for the ridiculous sum of money.         Later, 'DRAX' admitted that he didn't complete the conversion because         he thought the original Amiga music was boring. I must confess that he         has a point there." (JCH)

TITLE: Lady Lisa
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This tune was composed and then put on ice, only to be packed and         released at a much later date." (JCH)

TITLE: Last One
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The last tune I made in Laxity's player until Laxity told me to stop         using his player. I then began coding a new player system and later an         editor as well." (JCH)

TITLE: Little Test
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The second tune I did after 'Better late than never'. Most samples         were sampled from the Korg M1 using Commodore's own hardware sampler         which plugged into the cartridge port. It makes VERY extensive use of         ring modulation and hard sync." (JCH)

TITLE: Lonewolf
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The only tune made in the compromise player v07. The player was too         awkward to use any further." (JCH)

TITLE: L.L.L.
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The first tune made in Laxity's. Not 100% my own composition since I         left parts of the instruments and bassline intact (try to compare it         with /MUSICIANS/L/Laxity/Ikari_Intro_Song.sid)." (JCH)

TITLE: Mad4
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Maduplec of 'BUDS', a very prominent coder in the demo scene became         quite an alrounder in the later C64 days. Making close to everything         himself he painted the graphics, coded, composed and even made a music         editor with his own player. He sent me a version of it to me for         testing, and this is the result. The player takes very little         rastertime. I remember that when I sent him the tune he told me it was         'typically me'." (JCH)

TITLE: Maduplec3
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "It is a slow tune - today, I actually think it sounds best if you         play it a THREE times the speed in SidPlay instead of the usual TWO.         It has nothing to do with 'Maduplec' from 'Buds' other than the name         itself." (JCH)(#1)COMMENT: This tune is played at the original 2x speed.(#2)COMMENT: This tune is the same as tune #1, but is played at 3x speed.

TITLE: Maniac Mansion
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Maniac Mansion, Tune #1 [from the game] ARTIST: Chris Grigg & David LawrenceCOMMENT: "I was impressed with the titletune on 'Maniac Mansion', an adventure         game by LucasFilm (that was years before they changed their name to         LucasArts). However, the instruments were rubbish so I did my very own         version of it. At a silent part in the end of the tune I even added a         few notes of my own." (JCH)

TITLE: Maniaxion
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: Later used in the titlescreen of the game Pitfighter, (C) 1991 Domark.

TITLE: Martin #4
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Apart from using the drumset from the 'Batman'-tune, I experimented         with the pulse Martin Galway made in the 'Rambo' highscore tune."         (JCH)

TITLE: Mayday v3
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Stranded in Iowa ARTIST: Manfred MannCOMMENT: "Parts of the song was actually inspired by an old Manfred Mann song         called 'Stranded in Iowa'." (JCH)

TITLE: Memory I
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Even though it was composed in the same month as where the editor was         finished, it was put on ice only to be properly packed and released         some years later." (JCH)

TITLE: Michelle
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Another two-in-one tune, one of the better of that period. Especially         the last part is IMHO still nice." (JCH)

TITLE: Misjudge
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The second of the three tunes I did in the compromise player v19         which takes very little rastertime." (JCH)

TITLE: Modemtrading
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A silly little song I did in my modem trading days. If you listen         carefully you can hear a telephone ringing - followed by a modem         connecting." (JCH)

TITLE: Moonlight
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the very first song I ever composed. It happened on Aegis         Sonix on the Amiga. I remember I was very proud - today, I wonder         why..." (JCH)

TITLE: Multivoice #2
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Here I experimented with the idea of using arpeggio to simulate a lot         of voices. It didn't turn out too great, though." (JCH)

TITLE: Need You Tonight v1
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Need You Tonight [from Kick] ARTIST: INXSCOMMENT: "Conversion of the old Inxs hit. Later in 1989 I made another attempt         because the demogroup Jewels wanted a better conversion." (JCH)

TITLE: Need You Tonight v2
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Need You Tonight [from Kick] ARTIST: INXSCOMMENT: "The second conversion I did of this tune, ordered by 'Excell' from         the demogroup 'Jewels' as payment for giving me a great         sequencepacker. I put a lot of work into making the conversion         accurate." (JCH)

TITLE: No Birthday!
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Shorter version of 'Birthday' without the silly birthday song in the         beginning." (JCH)

TITLE: Ode to JO
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made after I heard one of JO's terrific 'hard restart' songs. I was         impressed with the way his ADSR worked on his chord sounds, so I tried         to do the same thing. However, I didn't really know what it was until         JO told me how it was done. I then implemented it from player v11."         (JCH)

TITLE: Ode to the 64
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I tried to make a tune like Rob Hubbard's 'One Man and his Droid',         but the result was not too brilliant." (JCH)

AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Funny tune with a ring modulation experiment. If you listen closely,         you can hear it say 'Give it up' - I thought it would be a nice touch         while shooting down enemies in the game. The ring modulation effects         appears from 00:16." TITLE: Orcus (guitaring)
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Here I used filtering on the leader to emulate a real guitar. The         EOLM tune is a very funny 'major' version. Imagine a bizarre monster         which looks like a clown. That tune is a conversion of a song which my         brother and I used to hum when we were kids..." TITLE: Orcus Intro
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Both this tune and the loader music reuses notes which I originally         composed in the titletune for the game. At the time of doing the music         for the game, I thought it would be a nice touch if a main theme could         be heard throughout the game - just like in the movies! :)" (JCH)(#1)   NAME: Intro Tune

AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A very weird theme for the tape loader - it uses parts of the same         composition as found in the titletune." (JCH)

TITLE: Paw Music (v2)
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "An introtune. The part from 00:20 was really a small excerpt from my         'Alpha Centauri'." (JCH)

TITLE: Pheric
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A tune using filtering in two voices which was not very common on the         C64. The tune was packed and released at a much later date." (JCH)

TITLE: Pit Fighter
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "One of the last game projects I worked on. Through the member in         Scotland, 'Deek', I made contact with a guy who managed to get me a         few orders from the software house 'Domark'. This music was ordered         for 'Pit Fighter'. It was probably in 1991 - I remember I made an         extra effort out of squeezing as many chords and effects into the two         voices of the ingame tune as I could, to make it sound like many more         voices." (JCH)         This game also uses /MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Maniaxion.sid(#1)   NAME: Bonus(#2)   NAME: Ingame

TITLE: Pit Pot
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Pit Pot ARTIST: <?>COMMENT: "Conversion from a game cartridge on the 8-bit SEGA. Sometimes it was         difficult to hear all the details which made me go for certain         compromises - something I was too inexperienced to handle properly at         that time..." (JCH)

TITLE: Playertest
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "As the name suggests a test of the miscellaneous functions in the new         player v20, like speed-, and pulse-programming test. This tune was of         course never spread." (JCH)

TITLE: Police
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Another old tune put on ice only to be released much later. It was         composed in a very fast speed setting." (JCH)

TITLE: Popcorn Remix
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: (#1)  TITLE: Popcorn [from Music To Moog By] ARTIST: Gershon KingsleyCOMMENT: "A remix made out of my own mind. And then not quite - the part in the         middle at 1:33 was inspired by 'Trollie Wallie' from Interceptor         Software (see /MUSICIANS/H/Hansford_Graham/Trollie_Wallie.sid)." (JCH)(#2)  TITLE: Popcorn [from Music To Moog By] ARTIST: Gershon Kingsley

TITLE: Problems
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Last experiment in the v00 series without effects." (JCH)

TITLE: Pseudo
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made in the 'Oswald' period." (JCH)

TITLE: Push-It
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The Danish demogroup 'Jewels' also fiddled with a puzzle game, called         'Push-It'. This is the intro tune, one of my favourite tunes from the         C64 period. It uses a double voice drum and was heavily inspired by         the music from 'Task III'. The game itself was never finished. You may         have to fiddle with filter parameters to make that snare drum sound         the way it should." (JCH)

TITLE: Push-It (main)
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Here's the main music block for 'Push-It', the puzzle game. It was         made in november 1989." (JCH)(#1)   NAME: Game Over(#2)   NAME: Hiscore(#3)   NAME: Ingame(#4)   NAME: Get Ready(#5)   NAME: Title Screen

TITLE: Quick Blast
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "One of the better tunes in the period with the old player system. It         was also the first tune to contain the typical 'Hubbard'-snare which         was a mixture of noise and triangle, swapped at each frame." (JCH)

TITLE: Rain Funk
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Released in a demo at the Randers copy-party, IMHO the very best C64         party there ever was." (JCH)

TITLE: Real ""Good""
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Named so because I liked the result when I made it in 1988/1989. I         remember I was so disappointed when I learned that 'Einstein' of         'Upfront' didn't like it." (JCH)

TITLE: Real Shit
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Actually extracted from a worktune called 'Cause I Love Her So'. I         liked the start of the worktune but I thought this part didn't really         belong so I extracted it to form a separate song and made a lot of         fast solo's on top of it." (JCH)

TITLE: Revenge
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Here I deliberately tried to put together a lot of chords in a song         which shifts in and out of the minor and major scales." (JCH)

TITLE: Revolutionary
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was the first tune done in the final editor, hence the name."         (JCH)

TITLE: Sampler #1
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: Contains four tunes. One of the tunes was extracted to form the single         tune "Hoppin'".(#4)COMMENT: This tune is almost identical to /MUSICIANS/J/JCH/Hoppin.sid

TITLE: Scanliner
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "First tune done in the compromise player v19. This player has no         vibrato routine at all." (JCH)

TITLE: Secret Land
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Secret Land [from Into a Secret Land] ARTIST: Sandra CretuCOMMENT: "Conversion of a hitsong from Sandra. I put a lot of work into making         the conversion accurate. Made just before the party in Slagelse."         (JCH)

TITLE: Shadow Sun
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was one of the last tunes I composed in an assembler listing. My         editor was almost complete and after trying it, I never wanted to         compose music in assembler again." (JCH)

TITLE: Sharks (game)
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The only real gametrack in the old player, containing 4 tunes. It was         ordered by a German democoder (Typhus of Inxs) but was never used."         (JCH)(#1)COMMENT: Titletune(#2)COMMENT: Ingame(#3)COMMENT: Hiscore(#4)COMMENT: Jingle

TITLE: She's Just a Maniac
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A tune where I tried to emulate the style of Maniacs of Noise. As the         title suggests, parts of the notes matches the words so you can         actually sing the title to it. Try it after 9-12 seconds of play! :)"         (JCH)

TITLE: Shift
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A worktune that wasn't finished. Due to the fact that we have reached         1991, my Korg M1 was a reality. This tune was totally composed on the         keyboard first, apart from the digi voice which was added later using         the editor alone. The digi voice doesn't appear until 01:16 - it was         supposed to be a 'surprise' tune. This was also the last digital tune         I did - and as far as I can remember, the very last C64 tune as well."         (JCH)

TITLE: Shorty
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Very short introtune made for a Dominators intro I coded myself."         (JCH)

TITLE: Short 'n' Sad
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus

TITLE: Skaermtrolden Hugo
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: TITLE: Hugo Rap [from Hugo Rap!] ARTIST: George Keller (Skaermtrolden Hugo)COMMENT: "A professional software house in Denmark called 'SilverRock' gained a         lot of success with 'Hugo' in danish television. This troll could be         controlled in a game using telephone buttons. A very new concept which         soon became enormously popular. During the success of the troll, a         real musician produced a CD containing a rap hit where Hugo was         singing using the typical voice which was also used in the game. As         the game was converted for sales versions from the Amiga to PC and         C64, I did the C64 song converted from the Danish rap hit." (JCH)

TITLE: Slapbass
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A long tune based on a slapbass. The result doesn't really sound like         a slapbass, but I couldn't get any closer at the time. Some years         later, a Dutch guy proved that by using the $51 waveform, you COULD         get quite close indeed!" (JCH)

TITLE: Song Made in Monitor

I was contacted and asked to do the soundtrack within a         very tight deadline. This is the music for the game - it was done in         march 1991." TITLE: Tecnetium
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I always get mixed feelings when I play this music. The title- tune         is long and I put a lot of work into it in april 1989, but today I can         hear loads of harmonic errors here and there. The game was done for a         sideways shoot'em up which a couple of totally unknown danish guys was         making. They soon lost all interest in their game, however. The         hiscore theme was a conversion of the old Cliff Richard hit         'Congratulations' done right out my head. I always wanted to make such         a hiscore tune, because I always thought Rob Hubbard did it all wrong         when he made 'sad' hiscore tunes. It is a sad thing when the game         ends, but getting a high score is supposed to be a GOOD thing! :)"         (JCH)(#1)   NAME: Title Screen(#2)  TITLE: Congratulations ARTIST: Cliff Richard

TITLE: Typhus #1
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the only tune I did in Future Composer, made at the Dexion         copy-party in 1988, the same party where I was told by Laxity to keep         my hands off his player. The Future Composer was a hack editor on         Charles Deenen's player and it arrived at this party for the first         time. I tried it out once - and never touched it again. 'Typhus' was         the name of the german guy who also ordered the 'Sharks' music in the         old player." (JCH)

TITLE: Voice
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "During my time of composing music I managed to own a C64 and a C128         at the same time. Naturally I just had to try the old experiment where         both computers are playing, echo detuning the music. This gave me the         idea of composing three voices on each computer to make 6 voices of         C64 music." (JCH)

AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus

TITLE: Who said Fred Grey?
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Very funny tune where I tried to emulate the weird 'pulsating' Fred         Grey used to have in his tunes where the pulse was changed for each         note but not during the note. As to whether I managed to match his         style or not - well, judge for yourself! :)" (JCH)

TITLE: Wizax Demo
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The first tune to use the 'testbit-noise' technique which locks and         unlocks the noise in such a way that the noise waveform sounds more         metallic. However, I later discovered that this worked differently         from C64 to C64. On some C64, I had to lock the waveform with $F0,         where other versions required $F8 to achieve the same effect." (JCH)

TITLE: X-Ray
AUTHOR: Jens-Christian Huus
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A trick introtune based on the idea of having a simple long filter         tone in very short intro's on the C64. I got this idea of playing such         a tone for some seconds, suddenly surprising everyone with a piece of         music." (JCH)

TITLE: 63 speed music #1
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Ray kept saying "Make more mutispeed music", so I did. Actully, it         only runs channel #1 at 63x, the other two channels run at 9x, but oh         well :). And it's too short... I very quickly got annoyed with the         unresponsiveness of the editor when trying to play sounds at this         rate. But I *do* like working with the sounds at these sort of update         rates, so I'm working on a player which takes a smaller amount of         raster time than TFX to use for such music. (That said, one of PCH's         TFX songs (supposedly) runs a channel at 72x, but that's just too         insane to dicuss :)." (JJ)

TITLE: Archnial
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The title of this song comes from my friend Jenn's AIM screenname,         whom I love dearly (in a completly plutonic way, for the record).         She doesn't understand the 'c64 thing'. I always wanted to be able to         write funk tunes like Drax, and later Mitch&Dane, do, and despite it         coming almost dead last in the c64.sk SID competition, I think I         succeeded somewhat. I actually like a lot of the harmonic work in         this song, as did my sister, who yelled at me after she first heard it         for being able to pull it off! Of course, most people disagreed with         her accusation of me pulling it off." (JJ)

TITLE: Archnial Triangle
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Someone on c64.sk made the statement that to do well, you need to         make songs which only use the triangle wave. So I did, and I think it         sounds a lot like something you'd hear on a NES. I actually prefer         this version myself." (JJ)

TITLE: Blood, Starlight, Rain...
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: NAME: Blood, Starlight, Rain Like Tears.COMMENT: "Sitting in a backpackers hostel in sydney, get a call from my         parents, I can't come home, they've rented out my room. I've been here         for 5 weeks now, but only finally got a laptop this day. I was feeling         incredibly dark, having spent the last week in bed ill, I really         wanted to go home, or failing that, I wanted someone to take a few         minutes out of their day to see if I was still alive (okay, so I was         feeling kind of melodramatic, lol),  This girl promised to hang out         with me, and then cancelled or forgot every time for weeks straight,         and I was stupid (read: thinking with my heart instead of my head)         and didn't want to acknowlage that she was ignoring me... I was         losing my mind, and this music represents that.         The full verse is "Blood, Starlight, Rain like tears, Drink from         this, and let go the years". I don't know who penned those words, but         I dropped the latter half from the title because I promised said girl         that I would.         This music was made on an emulator (vice 1.8, and of course I had         resid turned on :-p). It was also one of my bigger expermients with         filters synced from different channels to the one they're targetting.         If it works at all on a real C64, I'd consider myself very lucky, lol,         because I didn't have access to one at the time." (JJ)

TITLE: Colors
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I sat down to create an ending music for the WOW demo 'Evolution',         with this text that I'd just written in my mind, and eight hours         later, I had most of this. It isn't (deliberatly) covering anything,         the resemblence to some other music is just a coincidence :).         Ironically, this is one of my happiest musics, and yet at the time I         made it, I was depressed and suicidal. Life is full of contrasts, I         guess that's what makes it special.         Well, that and Ray finally fixing the restart bug in TFX :-p." (JJ)

TITLE: Eternal Skies
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was inspired by a song named "Eternal" by Evanescence. It was         originally going to be a cover of said song, however that went awry         within the first 10 seconds or so :). The second half is mostly an         experiment in what happens when you mix diffrent types of Ringmod and         Sync effects, which I like the sound of. Sidplay1 hates it. It was         originally intended to sound quite different from this, because the         original sketch for it required a dyanmic wave table, but I got fed up         waiting for that, and finished it as is." (JJ)

TITLE: Evolution
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I try, I fly, I lie, I cry, I die. My mis-understood epic. Everyone         except for Ray hated this :). It started out as soundmon clone music         (intended for the WOW demo of the same name), an evolution in music,         you know, the idea being that I've also got future composer type music         (see TFX == future composer), and the other guys were going to do         modern music blah blah watever, I forget the details. Anyhow, around         2 minutes after I sat down at the editor, it instead became something         else (I hate it when that happens :-p), which basically amounts to an         attempt to place what was goes through my mind at the time into SID         form... the evolution of my soul. I achieved that, I think, which is         probably why almost no-one else understands it. I personally like         this music better than any other which I have ever made, however my         emotional attachment to it makes me biased." (JJ)

TITLE: Exuding Titleness
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Exuding Titleness [from the Scream Tracker 3 module] ARTIST: Andrew Sega (Necros)COMMENT: "PG Gave me a copy of this on a CD when I was in the Czech Republic         during 2000, and I instantly fell in love with it, and as soon as I         arrived home to my C64, this cover of it was the first thing I did.         It was done in kind of a hurry, as I had other things on my mind, and         so it could be significantly better than it is, but it's still not         terrible, overall." (JJ)

TITLE: Fields of Innocence
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian
STILENTRY: TITLE: Fields of Innocence [from Origin] ARTIST: EvanescenceCOMMENT: "Only a partial cover... initially I set out to do a full cover of         this, however in the end I only covered the the lead and background         melodies (a few bars each), and then did my own music around that.         Kind of a waste, really, because the original is much better than I         could ever hope to achieve, but it's not bad compared to all of my         others, even if it is completly pale and lame compared to the         original. Jazzcat mislabled this "Fields of Hades" when it was used in         an issue of Vandalism News, but we still love him anyhow :-p." (JJ)

TITLE: Fishmagic
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "In another world, I am known as Fish. Felt like doing a cutesy         little tune one day. This is it. It's not terribly good, in         retrospect. The later sections continue my love affair with ring         modulation. It's too short, it's too lame, it's too cheesy, and I was         too tired to care. It relies kind of heavily on the semantics of a         6581 filter in places... on an 8580, some things just don't sound         quite right :(.         Anthony Bisset, from Digiradi/DSP Audio remixed this and layed vocals         over it." (JJ)(#1)COMMENT: 6581 version.(#2)COMMENT: 8580 version.

TITLE: Forever
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was inspired by the music from the PC demo 'Forever' by Acme. I         don't recall who did that music, but this doesn't actully sound much         at all like it... but you should listen to that music if you can find         it, because it's really good. There is another story that goes with         this music, which explains the in binary message, which starts, as         all good stories does, 'Well, there was this girl...' :). Her name         was Sonja, and she didn't.         But she was leaning over my shoulder when I was packing this tune, and         is the only girlfriend I've had who has even tollerated, let alone         understood, my C64 obsession. As a birthday surprise for me, she made         a C64 music. It was surprisingly good for a first ever SID piece!         One day, it may see the light of day, but today is not that day." (JJ)

TITLE: Game Over(view) #1
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was the music from the first ever Game Over(view), and was         written for it the day before it was released (at the start of 2004).         It was an attempt to do a song in the same style as Detert's Game On         11/93, and although it didn't quite turn out that way, I like how it         ended up." (JJ)

TITLE: Green Hill
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: You Can Do Anything (Toot Toot Sonic Warr.) [from the GG game Sonic 2] ARTIST: Masafumi OgataCOMMENT: "I beat this game in a couple of hours when it first came out, but         always loved the music, and this tune in particular. Fast forward to         mid 2000, and I'm sitting in a backpackers hostel in Prague with my         gamegear, and I have no alarm clock and a 9am flight to catch, with my         girlfriend (who I hadn't seen for 5 months) is waiting on the other         end of it. So hence I can't really go to sleep (I'd die if I missed         said flight :-p), but hey, I have a gamegear with this game, and so I         play until Green Hill zone, and then listen to this music for 7 hours         straight, at which point I finally ran out of spare lives and         continues.         Fast forward to June/July 2001, and I've got some weird illness where         I can't stand up or hold down food (never did work out what the was,         heh), and my girlfriend runs away to america because the idea that         for once in her life she has to be an adult is to damned hard to deal         with (Hey, Gundam Wing Hentai is much more fun), and I havn't slept         for 2 weeks or eaten in 4 weeks (not an exaggeration), which has had         the predictable effects on my mind. Crawl over to my C64, load TFX,         bury myself of memories of that night in Prague and happy fun music!         Only digital love is eternal." (JJ)

TITLE: Happy Happy! Joy Joy!
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Despite my first C64 music being made in 1988, this is probably the         first one I did which wasn't complete and utter crap (Well, maybe this         and "Not so JCH based", but it was done on a bad emulator and breaks         on a real C64, it turns out ^_^. Maybe one day I'll remake it and         release it, because the ideas in it were good, just bad implentation         as is the usual thing with me :). It wasn't until later that year         the the message penetrated my brain that, if you want to make an         okay music, you need to spend more than an hour on it ;). If I was         running WOW, I would have kicked me out for being completly lame ;).         But hey, I learned my lesson (sort of....)" (JJ)

TITLE: Internalise
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was inspired by what I remembered of Ash Hogg's Spellcast title         music, however it turns out that even the part I thought I'd stolen         (the background lead that plays at the start) bears not much         resemblence to it. Go figure. This is another music, like evolution,         which is really a reflection of my psyche at the time, however this         one didn't get the negative reaction which evolution did :). People         did tell me that it's too short, however, and they're right. But cest         la vie.         A shame that I couldn't make a really big and fearsome snare,         though..." (JJ)

TITLE: Midi Drums
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Midi Drums [from the midi module] ARTIST: Jaymz JulianCOMMENT: "This is the second attempt I made to do this song on the C64, and was         in fact the song that TFX table variables were created for. I         originally tried to do this in Sid Duzz It in early 1999, but the         number of arpeggio commands required for the places where there is         two leads in one channel, and the blips in the drum/bass channel,         overwelmed that editor. So I tried in JCH v20g4, where I had managed         to succed with Sunset Spirals, due to the ability it has to change the         wavetable from within a song, but this too was not to be, due to the         limitations of the editor. So, I started writing a new editor, which         was specifically designed to handle this situation, by splitting each         channel into six virtual channels, and using special rules to modulate         them together. But this took up a lot of ram and raster time, indeed         it too so much ram in the editor that I could only store five patterns         at a time, so this was not to be either. So Ray introduced me to TFX,         and I asked him about changing the wave table from within the song,         but he wouldn't have this, because it would confuse people, but he         suggested a viable alternative, which is to support variables in the         wave table, and promised to add this feature asap. That was January         2001, but he was too busy to implement them for the next two and a         half years. So I started bugging him to just give me the source and         the bits to build it, and in November 2003, he did. So, I put my         money where my mouth was, and added that feature (and a bunch of         others which I had been wanting for a long time), and I was _finally_         able to do a version of this that I happy with. To anyone else but         me, this is just another mediocre game tune, but for me it was an         achievement." (JJ)

So, my         version is crap too, but I think it has the nice harmonies in the         second half, at least, and I think is a little less crap than his :)."         (JJ)

TITLE: Purple Sky
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Purple Sky II [from the Scream Tracker 3 module] ARTIST: Jonne Valtonen (Purple Motion of Future Crew)COMMENT: "After Sunset Sprirals, I was once again fed up with JCH's editor, and         wanted something better. Ray had suggested to me using TFX several         times before, and I finally got some documentation for it, and so now         was the time to use it. I had the S3M of this kicking around, and so         I covered it to learn the editor. The instruments suck... I never was         good at making percussion, and unfortunantly there isn't any good ones         around made in TFX to rip. I also had basically zero understanding of         how the wave tables worked when I did this, and as a result there are         some very stupid things in there which sound terrible ;). This         probably should never have been released, but people liked it for         reasons that I don't understand.         As it turned out, the instruments sounded so crap partially because         Ray's player was horrifically bugged, at the time. I recompiled it         against a later player, and it sounds a LOT better." (JJ)

TITLE: Rasterman
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Flop Magazine 41 [from the Atari XL/XE music] ARTIST: Radek Sterba (Raster)COMMENT: "So, TFX 2.9 still wasn't here, but I wanted to cover this 4 channel         music from the atari, so what I did, is set the player to 1 frame per         row, and then enter all of the arpeggios by hand. I'm surprised it         didn't make the file much larger than it is. It was a pain in the         ass, but I'm quite pleased with the result." (JJ)

TITLE: Rekonstruct
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This song is made up entirely of patterns from Fishmagic, but played         a different tempo's and in a differnet order. It was originally         intended to be used in a demo with fishmagic, so I was going for that         similar but different effect, and I think it worked very well. But,         ironically, I was never happy enough with the original fishmagic, or         how the demo was turning out, so I gave this to Jazzcat for an issue         of Vandalism News, for which it was much more suitable anyhow. I love         this sort of song, why don't people do more of them?" (JJ)

TITLE: Sonic Dreams
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was my entry for the 2004 SidWine competition, and it did         fantasitcally badly, despite being what I consider to be probably the         best demoscene style song that I've done on the C64. I actually spent         a lot of time on this song, and I was quite proud of how it turned out         when it was finished. It makes extensive use of the TFX wave table         variables to try and squeeze two melody lines into a single channel,         and the NoPulse command to control pulse width modulation reset more         finely.         The song is dedicated to a group I used to be a part of, Sonic Dreams,         which is another story." (JJ)

TITLE: Sunset Spirals
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (Coder)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Sunset Spirals [from the Impulse Tracker module] ARTIST: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)COMMENT: "This is, musically, probably the best thing that I have ever done on         the C64. Ironically, all of my C64 friends complained that it was off         key, etc, and all of my PC friends love this version. Yet I had         exactly the opposite reaction to the original version (c64 guys tended         to like it, pc guys tended to complain that it was off key.). For the         record, except for one or two notes, because I ran out of arpeggios (I         do that a lot... there are two or three other musics which got         scrapped half way through because I ran out of arpeggios. Thankfully,         we've come up with a solution to this in the new version of TFX :)),         the notes are NOT off key, and I don't care what you all think :-p.         Said PC guys decided to take ownership of this song, and wanted me to         create more like it, but I havn't had the motivation to actully         finish any of them. (There are many, many, many stories that I could         tell about the digiradi guys, but that's for another day, but the         credit of the music to "Coder" is a part of that insanity. They were         great times)." (JJ)

TITLE: Tim Got High
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian & Edward R. Jones
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The Tim in question is Tim Bray, who does an act "Casionova", where         he shows off 80's home keyboards, and other chip instruments,         including a Commodore 64 with a guitar strap attached. Loscha and I         were at one of his gigs, and he was tanking really badly (indeed, we         could remember more of the words to his songs than he could!). This         was mostly because, we think, he was completly off the planet. So, we         came back to my place, after the gig, and I was showing off the new         version of TFX, and we wrote the bass/chord/drum line (which is all         one channel) to demonstrate some of the new features. The file needed         a name, and so we just typed in "Tim got high", and the name stuck.         This song also has a lot of ring modulation (Joxstrap/WOW said too         much :-p), which I love as always." (JJ)

TITLE: Winter's Dream
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Winter's Dream [from the Impulse Tracker module] ARTIST: Andrew Sega (Necros)COMMENT: "Back when I was writing music on the PC for 16 hours a day, every         day, this was the demo song included with one of the many "this is the         last release really!" releases of impulse tracker. I'd actually         wanted to make a C64 version of this for a long time, but it took me         until now to really work out how to do it to my liking.         Throwing that piece of junk away to concentrate on C64 music was the         best descision I ever made. I never was very good at it, anyhow."         (JJ)

TITLE: Yawlag Xard Hcj!
AUTHOR: Jaymz Julian (A Life in Hell)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the only released music made in the modified version of JCH's         player that I was hacking up during 1999 (I had all of my stuff         stolen, including the only copy of the player sources etc). I         originally wanted to create Galway style tune, but changed my mind         half way and thought I'd make a Drax style music instead, and then put         a JCH style lead on it. Read the title backwards, and it will all         make sense. This was also the first music of mine that I know of to be         used in someone else's production (of course *I* use my own music, but         well, it's crap, so no-one else does), which was a graphic collection         by someone in Sonic Dreams (Rat I think). Those guys were great fun,         and some of them actully liked my music, which was a nice change, but         goddamn the organisation of that group turned into a clusterfuck :-p,         But it was all fun at the end of the day." (JJ)

TITLE: FRODIGI
AUTHOR: Naveed Khugiani (Algorithm)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This demonstrates a new method of playing back digitized samples.         It demonstrates the output of my new audio encoder that produces         output that is able to be decoded on the C64 using only a few raster         lines per frame. It uses the free running SID oscillators on the C64's         SID chip in 3 channels and a master volume to recreate the audio.         Mainly suited for speech, but can also work on other sources. TITLE: I.C.U.P.S.
AUTHOR: Barry Leitch
STILENTRY: TITLE: Hoodoo Voodoo ARTIST: Graham Marsh (BOGG)COMMENT: "Icups - my first published work... I had written the tune as a demo,         and I had been trading with Bogg for a few years, and I had re-written         his tune just to see how I would have taken his initial idea and run         with it myself. Anyways, I had sent disks with a load of tunes on to         all the major software companies at the time. Firebird contacted me,         they wanted to use Icups. I told them at the time that it was kind of         a rip off of Bogg's Detergent, but they were quite happy to offer to         buy it. They offered me 150 pounds, and then when someone pointed out         again to them that it was based on Bogg's tune, they gave him half the         money too which I was quite happy with." (BL)

TITLE: Air on a Rasterline
AUTHOR: Linus Åkesson (lft)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The tune is remarkable from a technical point of view, because the         playroutine only needs 63 clock cycles (one rasterline) per frame,         whereas a normal playroutine needs around 24 rasterlines. To put that         in perspective, consider that simply calling the playroutine (jump to         subroutine + return from subroutine) uses up 12 cycles, i.e. almost 20%         of the available time. Obviously this severely limits the number of         features the player can support; there's no vibrato, no arpeggios, and         so on. Still, it was fun to try to work musically within those extreme         constraints.         This project then went on to inspire Hermit Soft to create One         Rasterline Tracker, a tool that lets non-coders take part in the fun.         However, his playroutine is not quite down to 63 cycles yet, and         believe me, the last few are the hardest. Still, it's a great         achievement!" (LA)

TITLE: The Chase (Midnight Express)
AUTHOR: Markus Klein (LMan)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Chase [from the movie Midnight Express] ARTIST: Giorgio MoroderCOMMENT: "Back then in 1991, the c64 was pretty much alive for me for I had no         money for buying an amiga... but in that time my ambitions and desires         for making music rose! Since having no sequencer or other audio gear         except my Roland M5, I started doing c64 SIDs using a program called         AMP. It allowed to compose in a tracker-like environment, and had a         nice interface for creating sounds. I tried to learn several techniques         by covering Hubbard's Commando, but my best SID was a cover of Moroder's         Midnight Express." (LMan)

TITLE: Giana Sisters DS
AUTHOR: Markus Klein (LMan)
STILENTRY: TITLE: The Great Giana Sisters, Tune #1 ARTIST: Chris HülsbeckCOMMENT: Remake of "Giana Sisters DS - Title Theme", by Fabian del Priore, from         the Nintendo DS version of the game released in 2009.         "This is a remake of the beautiful title tune from Giana Sisters for         the Nintendo DS, released 2009. The tune was composed and arranged by         Fabian del Priore aka Rapture, and is itself a cover of Chris         Hülsbeck's original Giana Sisters Title Theme.         I contacted Rapture about my intent to recreate the tune on a stock         c64. He liked the idea and kindly provided the original audio source         files. My challenge was to port every little detail from the original         and make it fit the limits given by the c64's hardware.         The music engine was coded by THCM, with the SID part done in         CheeseCutter, and the sample part in OpenMPT." (LMan)

STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Kind of a sequel to 'Jump Around', as it features a lot of the same         stuff. It has a tiny bit of PVCF to it (ARFGHHH!!)....... Excuse me, I         have to Vommit! It must have been a mistake. Did I do that... Hand me         some valium... NOW!... Someone PLEASE erase this tune... Turn it         off... Delete... DO SOMETHING!" (TH)

TITLE: Flaciied
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v13.         This tune is kind of a cover of a Reyn Ouwehand tune he had done in         Music Assembler - well, the chords are the same..." (TH)

TITLE: Flopper 2
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A tune, which I did just before my old C64 burned out. The tune got         lost when I moved to Aalborg, but fortunately Syndrom had the tune."         (TH)

TITLE: Funcommie
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A tune building on the chords used in the last part of my PC-tune         called Trilogy. The tune however is totally different." (TH)

TITLE: Fusion
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This tune was completed just before the Sams0 party in Denmark during         the summer of 1992. I got Steve/ex-Xfactor to deliver this tune to the         music competetion - however, I've never heard nor seen any results         from that party, so I really haven't got a clue as to how it did...         The tune itself is a combination of early C64-techno and some strange         stuff - hence the name 'Fusion'!" (TH)

TITLE: Garrison
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         Another one of those early tunes in the NP-players, which really don't         need any comments..." (TH)

TITLE: Gedefims
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         This is probably one of my most used tunes. Back in 1990, when it was         made, I think it got used in 3 or 4 demos. The tune was composed         immediately after listening to a Charles Deenen tune for some         race-game (forgot the name). I made a conversion of it on the Amiga,         which never got released." (TH)

TITLE: Geologic
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Ahh... Mot many liked this tune I guess. I didn't get much response to         it, when it was in Skyhigh #19 - perhaps it was caused by an error in         the coding of the outfit which caused the tune to sound like crap... I         guess you could say this tune was heavily inspired by Jamiroquai."         (TH)

TITLE: Gravöl
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         The title for this one is also Danish and means funeral-beer... It was         actually an attempt to do something in a similar style as JCH.         However, I think this tune without any doubt is 100% Metal. The tune         has never been used - not to my knowledge anyway..." (TH)

TITLE: Groovin' High
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         I converted this tune from Drax and Laxity's PC-version. Just couldn't         resist it, as it was such a cool tune." (TH)

TITLE: Hiscore
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: TITLE: a.hiscore [from the Amiga MOD module] ARTIST: Jesper KydCOMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         A tune converted from Amiga. It's originally made by Jesper Kyd and         was featured in a Silents demo. I converted this in the summer of         '91." (TH)

TITLE: Hotshot
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v15.         I did this tune exclusively for my pal Morpheus/Flash Inc. for his mag         Hotshot. I think it was used in 2 or 3 issues in the intro. This tune         is not the one used in Hotshot though, as I changed the filters a bit.         Hot V2.0 is the 'real' tune. Anyway, I thought this should be included         as well as I bothered to spread it." (TH)

TITLE: Hotshot v2
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v15.         This is the 'real' version of Hotshot M. with the filters changed a         bit." (TH)

TITLE: Incoqnito
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A fast composed tune which I made especially for Iceball/Motiv8 to use         in his game 'Tric Trac' or so... As usual I never got the money for         it, as the fantastic incredible Cherry Software managed not to pay."         (TH)

TITLE: Introjam
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v10.         Another tune from 1989 which was meant as an intro-tune for Contex,         but it never made it, and I think to this date it's never been used."         (TH)

TITLE: Jensemand
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         I kinda named this tune after JCH, not that the tune itself has         anything to do with him... It's just like with most of my work - fuck         the name, it's the tune that counts." (TH)

TITLE: JozzMatazz
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A tune, which Johannes Bjerregaard has been composing in the         MIDI-format. It's fairly different from what Johannes usually did on         C64." (TH)

TITLE: Jump'round
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Sitting at my synth I came up with these chords, and thinking         immediately that they would suit a house-tune just perfectly I did         this tune. It's fairly simply, but then again so is all house-music.         It has a catchy theme though I think. Lion/Chromance used this for the         intro for Domination #8. The tune was supposed to be exclusive, but         then suddenly out of the blue an old AVT-project called 'Icarus'         surfaced, and as my tune was first intended for that production I was         quite annoyed by this. Who thought an AVT-production would turn up as         a Padua*Hitmen production. Oh well, fuck that." (TH)

TITLE: Kedsomehed
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         A tune inspired a bit by rock'n'roll. Anyway as far as I know it was         used in an Abnormal crack-intro by Stone, I think - however they         screwed up the credits as it was credited to Torben Larsen instead of         the correct Torben Hansen or simply Metal... But who cares about that         now..." (TH)

TITLE: Köleskab
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         I made this tune in December 1991 especially for the upcoming Lethal         Display 4, but I ended up delivering if to Steve/X-factor, as he had         just started his software label called Imagination Developments. So,         at The Party 1 in 1991 he got the finished tune and plugged it into         the demo, which was then released... Syndrom liked this tune so much         that he did a 90% copy of it. He explained to me later on, that he did         it to gain experience, which is OK my me, but unfortunately it got         used in game for which Syndrom got some money... Anyway, we've         straightened that out long ago. BTW, the title means Fridge." (TH)

TITLE: Legoklods
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Haha, well, this tune is basically built totally on one of my other         tunes, namely 'Geologic' - the chords are the same, but the rest         differs. Exclusive for DOMINATION #9 Magazine outfit." (TH)

TITLE: Lethalic
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         Made this especially for the intro-sequence of Lethal Display 3,         however, I think my work was a total waste considering the final         result of it. Anyway the 3rd tune is ok." (TH)

TITLE: MF 2DD XL
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v10.         This tune was my first in the NP-V10. It was made in 1989, and I think         it was featured in one of Walt's screens in Lethal Display 3 (the         circle scroller)." (TH)

TITLE: Microcosm
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Hmm... Some chords I came up with while playing around on the keys...         And the rest was basically rushed together. I guess the tune is OK,         but I really think it's way too boring." (TH)

TITLE: (Mon)iacs
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         Inspired by Jeroen Tel's tune for Tintin on the Moon, I sat down and         put this together in a relative short time. I got a lot of good         response on this tune, and I also think it's quite catchy. I think it         was used in Lethal Display 3... or at least it's been used in some         other demos." (TH)

TITLE: Morpheus
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         My old friend Morpheus/Flash Inc. wanted me to do a tune named after         him, and after a while I did. Unfortunately my timing was lousy, as         Morpheus had left the scene when I had finished the tune, ofcoz         meaning that it had never been used. Too bad really." (TH)

TITLE: Mums #1
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This is basically another intro-like-tune. It's nothing special."         (TH)

TITLE: Mystic
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This tune was made after fiddling around on my synth. I came up with         the scales that sounded very mystical... Hence the name. It's very         short really, and think that Avantgarde got to use it in an intro."         (TH)

TITLE: Nedsat psyko
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: Nearly the same as /MUSICIANS/M/Metal/Psykologic.sid

TITLE: Nosefuck
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A nice and short bossanova-like tune, which I did in 1993 after         getting myself a new C64." (TH)

TITLE: Note-It 1
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A series of chords and BAM! you have a tune... Well, this was         originally only a work-tune, but I dug it out from the dungeons and         finished it rather rapidly thinking it would probably suit some         note..." (TH)

TITLE: Note-It 2
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This tune - as you may be able to hear - has a few sequences similar         to the ones in Note-it 1. That's simply because I built this tune from         Note-it 1 - adding some other chord-theme and yet another note-tune         was done... I should probably never have released these 2 tunes as I         really think they stink..." (TH)

TITLE: Ode 2 Riis
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Odd, coz this tune is dedicated to Bjarne Riis (who?!) - after         achieving 3rd place in the Tour de France in 1995... Who should've         known he would win the darn race the year after... Oh well, this tune         was used in one of The Pulse, when it returned in 1995." (TH)

TITLE: Oh Baby
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Let's Hear It for the Boy ARTIST: Deniece WilliamsCOMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         I converted this tune from a Walkman tune [Lets Hear My Baby] on         the Amiga. Walkman was definitely one of the best composers on the         Amiga during my time on the Amiga. JCH liked this conversion even         though I found it a bit dull compared to the original." (TH)

TITLE: Orbital
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Mitch/Crest/Hype! had been composing another funky-tune and during one         of our talks he asked me if I couldn't do a techno-thingie using the         same chord structure. And well, here's the result. I think         Deff/ex-Avantgarde wanted to use it in a graphics-collection, but that         didn't go well at all." (TH)

TITLE: Organic
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This is one half of a Jeroen Tel tune and one half myself. Actually         after listening to it a number of times I kinda like my parts more.         Oh well... Judge for yourself. I believe this tune was featured in the         end-screen in one of the 1st (if not the last) Flash Inc. demo.         Hmm..." (TH)  TITLE: Supremacy, Tune #1 (0:00-1:13) ARTIST: Jeroen Tel  TITLE: National Anthem of the Soviet Union (1:28-1:36) ARTIST: Aleksandr Aleksandrov  TITLE: Supremacy, Tune #1 (1:55) ARTIST: Jeroen Tel

TITLE: Parrot
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v15.         The name of this tune came from a disk I got from JCH. On the cover         there was an ugly parrot... Well, the tune is OK, I guess. It was used         by Kwon, or at least it was supposed to. Hmm... My memory kinda         sucks." (TH)

TITLE: Plasma 5
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v11.         After finishing this tune, I felt that it was too slow and boring, but         Walt told me that he thought it was great and he used it in the         Raytrace-part of Crackle'n'Cocio for the Daniaz party in 1990."         (TH)

TITLE: Plastic T
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         After finishing this tune I was pretty sure that no-one had done         anything remotely like this on the C64. Ofcoz I was wrong, but still I         think it's one of the first techno-tunes in the scene. I think it was         used in a crack-intro for Regina." (TH)

TITLE: Please Me
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Please me [from the Amiga MOD module] ARTIST: Kim Tolstrup Christensen (Future Freak)COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         I came across a music-disk on the Amiga from Future Freak/Dexion, and         on that disk there was a fabulous tune called 'Please me', and I         thought it was such a great, that I simply had to do a conversion of         it - ofcoz the original sounds alot better, but still... Unfortunately         it's never been used." (TH)

TITLE: Profile
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v11.         I had read way too many Dragonlace books when I made this... It was         used in the end-part in Crackle'n'Cocio." (TH)

TITLE: Psykologic
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: Nearly the same as /MUSICIANS/M/Metal/Nedsat_psyko.sid

TITLE: Ramlösa
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Ahh... A cool refreshing Ramlosa beats almost everything after a         fierce battle on the soccer-field. Anyway, this tune is rather wierd -         at least the first part is kinda strange. I'm not sure if it ever got         used by anyone, which I think is a darn shame." (TH)

TITLE: Ray-Ban
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Actually this tune is one of the first where I actually played some         chords on a piano before composing. It's a fairly melodic tune."         (TH)

TITLE: Resigning
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         Silly as I am, I thought this tune was my last one on the C64...         ...Well, just take a look at the amount of tunes dated after this         one... I don't think I resigned after all. :)" (TH)

TITLE: Revealed
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Well, as the title 'reveals' this tune was meant for the Camelot         magazine Revealed. The tune would have suited an intro just as well, I         think, but Kring decided after Revealed #3 to make the following issue         a cyber-like issue, and so I had to compose some deep techno."         (TH)

TITLE: S-Depress
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v11.         Ah... Sounds a bit like... well, Drax actually. At this time my style         was heavily influenced by Drax, as we met quite a lot. This tune was         used in an X-Factor production - can't remember the name, but it's an         old thing. I don't think it was used in any Bonzai productions, but         then again, I might be wrong." (TH)

TITLE: Sayonara
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         This tune is featured in the intro of the Bonzai demo 'Bonzieed'. I         put this together at the Bonzai meeting at THA's place in the summer of         1990. To my knowledge it hasn't been used in other productions." (TH)

TITLE: Schwantz
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         Argh, this tune kinda marks the beginning of an era of my compositions         - the strange year(s)... An era which really isn't over, but I'm not         half as strange as I was at this time..." (TH)

TITLE: Shaolink
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         Again, an Amiga conversion. This time I converted Jochen Hippel's tune         for Shaolin. It was in a really lame FM-editor on the Amiga." (TH)

TITLE: Shit It
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         Hmm... Another tune from 1989 - yuck. Though, it has a bit of that         speed-freak attitude that some of my later work has." (TH)

TITLE: Sidekick
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         An attempt to create a Hybrid between C64-heavy metal and just         something speedy... Deff loved one and made me do a sequel         (Deaf-Deff), which IMO didn't really turn out as good as this one... I         think this tune is one of my longest, as I think it goes for some 5-6         minutes." (TH)

TITLE: Skumbanan
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A little tune which I composed in some 2 hours or so... It's an ok         tune, but it's fairly boring..." (TH)

TITLE: Smal Sag
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         Another one of those tunes that was just floating around on one of my         work-disks, and - as usual - I packed and this one ever got spread,         but I'm not sure if it was ever used." (TH)

TITLE: Sofakoger
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Boiling in your couch. That's basically what this is all about. I made         this exclusively for SCS*TRC. I hope they used it in their intros :)"         (TH)

TITLE: Soft Eyes
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         I made this tune in a hurry for Trap's 18th birthday demo back in         1990. I don't think it's been used in other productions since." (TH)

TITLE: Swingin'
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         This tune is one of those tunes which has been used a lot. It was         originally featured in the fractal-part of the Bonzai demo called         Crackle'n'Cocio that won the Daniax party in 1990." (TH)

TITLE: Teknolog
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This was the 3rd tune featured in Revealed #4. It's a mix of a         Jam&Spoon tune and some of my own stuff... It also has been used for a         game, with my permission, but unfortunately I got no money for it -         typical!!" (TH)

TITLE: Telefax
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v14.         Inspired by a simple thing as the telephone signal, I wrote this tune         (my own phone, actually). The rest of the tune came out quite well,         and it was one of my fave tunes for a long time. MSK told me that it         was the best tune he had ever heard... Hmm.. Anyway, it was used in         the 1st part in Crackle'n'Cocio." (TH)

TITLE: Time 4 Sex
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v15.         One of those tunes you stumble upon when listening through your work         disks. Just packed the damn thing because it sounded special. Didn't         pack it for any particular reason." (TH)

TITLE: Tjuhej
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         A tune that sounds much like it's name. I think it's a rather merry         tune and I like it somewhat more then the usual tunes I've made. I         believe the tune was used by Walt in the 1st Starion demo called         'Oksen' from 1993." (TH)

TITLE: Törstig
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         The title of this tune means 'Thirsty!' - don't ask me why as it has         absolutely nothing to do with the tune itself... Silly me as usual."         (TH)

TITLE: Toxicjazz
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         I made this tune especially for a music-contest conducted by the group         Life/Riffs. I know that Drax and Laxity competed aswell, but no one         ever knew who won... Oh well, this tune basically sucks, so I don't         think it stood a chance against the other tunes in that competition."         (TH)

TITLE: Triiix!
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Another merry tune, but rather simple tune, which was used by Walt in         the Starion demo 'Oksen' from 1993." (TH)

TITLE: Trip 2 Jupiter
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This is another tune made on the same weekend as the other two 'Trip 2         x' tunes. Read text for 'Trip 2 Mars' for more details." (TH)

TITLE: Trip 2 Mars
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         Oh yes! This is one of my faves as well. I made this and the other 2         'Trip 2 x' tunes during the one single weekend, as Kring/Camelot         wanted some strange cyber stuff for his Revealed magazine (issue 4 -         the last!). Somehow he ended up only using 2 of the 'Trip 2 x'-tunes,         where this tune unfortunately was the rejected one. Hmf... Not that         this tune bears no resemblence to my PC tune carrying the same name         (it's even better). Playing it on a new SID gives the best result!!"         (TH)

TITLE: Trip 2 Pluto
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v20.         This is another tune made on the same weekend as the other two 'Trip 2         x' tunes. Read text for 'Trip 2 Mars' for more details." (TH)

TITLE: Turbojam
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         A fast beat - some chords and a horrible lead... Together it describes         my first tunes very well. I did this tune shortly after getting the         NP-Players from JCH." (TH)

TITLE: TWINE End
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: TITLE: The World is not Enough [from the movie] ARTIST: Garbage

TITLE: Virginize
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         A nice little tune, which I originally composed for mine and Drax's         music group called Unitech Designs, but I never got around to code         another one of those music demos. The 3 Unitech demos that we did         release all included Drax's tunes." (TH)

TITLE: Vommit!
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v17.         Oh dear... Another strange tune... Never used. Quiz time! Guess why         the tune is called Vommit.. yes, correct answer - I was boozing the         night before and felt soo bad the day after that I actually commited         during composing this tune... hehe... Also did that during a composing         session with Drax on the game-project 'Lollypop'... Talk about a         strange source of inspiration!" (TH)

TITLE: Weird!
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v15.         Made this tune especially for the demo Crackle'n'Cocio, it was used in         the x-y-z logo zoomer part. The tune caused a massive positive         feedback - I guess they liked it." (TH)

TITLE: What Now?
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v18.         Together with Hiscore, Einstein, Ray-ban and Cream, this tune was         supposed to be sold to a Polish group called Axis - however, the deal         was never really on as they didn't have any money. Tough luck. ;) I         think this tune is inspired by a Laxity track (guess which one for         yourself!)." (TH)

TITLE: Wild Talk
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with JCH Newplayer v9.         We don't need to talk too much about this one - just another of those         early tunes made in 1989." (TH)

TITLE: Xmas Beat
AUTHOR: Torben Hansen (Metal)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made with Newplayer v11.         I remember having made this just before Xmas in 1989 and I brought it         along to the Dominators-Trilogy-Upfront party in Randers, where the         Contex gang heard it - and guess what - they actually liked it... I         used it in my Music-Collection (the one that never got released...         Gmm...)" (TH)

TITLE: Anosognosia
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Anosognosia [from NecroLepsy] ARTIST: NecroPoloCOMMENT: GMC2.0 "It has a twisty story. The original song was created in         2012 when I started to create prototype mixing sessions that         became the base of my albums AENTHERA (2016), HYPERGAME (2017)         and DESTRONNAUTH (2019). Virtually this one was the very first         demo track that I made for the upcoming chip-metal albums,         other tracks were just finished first. Finally it had its place         on the 4th album called NECROLEPSY (2022). At the moment of         releasing this SID in 2021 the album hasn't been even mixed down         yet so the SID cover version created for Vincenzo's C64 Grand         Tour Challenge became the first public release." (NP)

TITLE: Anticitizen 64
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: defMON "There are tools that completely re-arrange the playfield.         defMON by Frantic is so much such. During Vincenzo's C64 Grand Tour         Challenge this was my favourite tracker. It was like driving a UFO         and jumping in and out dimensions. The title is a reference to         Gordon Freeman from Half-Life2. defMON is a dimension jumper anyway         so it is a good fit." (NP)

TITLE: Arthrobob
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: 1RT1.0 "Originally it was a test file of Hermit's 1-RasterTracker.         Before the release time, Knut asked Vincenzo if he could make a SID         for his return one-part demo made for DOTY2013. Vincenzo did not         have any time so he passed the project to me. At that moment I had         only this raw little SID in the hatch. Finally it appeared to be         a very nice fit to Knut's awesome bob demo part that uses perfect         synch to the music." (NP)

TITLE: Berzerk Redux Loader
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: MS2.1 "Tune has a long way home: initially it existed as an audio         track for an iPhone race game called "Freeway'86". The game had a         C64 style mode so original SID sounds were to be included. For that         I created six or seven of SID worktunes and some short jingles. The         game did not reach the finish line so most of tunes eat dust. For         Martin's MS2 online compo I fed the music data of the "Coastal"         subtune into the proggie. Checking the tune, Martin asked if he         can use it for the loading screen of Berzerk Redux cart version.         It is one of my fav new-old games so I was really happy to provide         that." (NP)

TITLE: Bluesbird
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)

I had         a phone/note book to keep some order in the mess. 20 years later         this book became my only memory of certain songs. According to it,         I still have 40-50 disks lurking around somewhere. This short tune         was hiding on one of the retrieved old disks and as archives say         it's one of my earliest SIDs." (NP)
