TITLE: Commodore from Hell
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: SW1.4 "I made the original track of this MIDI conversion for a         retro style PC racing game called Project Downforce around 2011.         The original sounded like an old chiptune from some SNES machine         so SID sound is not too far from its original form, just longer.         A couple of years later Jazzcat asked a rocking SID for a dismag         and I expanded the original tune, using Hermit's SWMconvert tool         that he made for SIDwizard. The title refers to legendary PANTERA         guitarist Dimebag Darrell. All the riffs and solos reflect his         style, I guess he would make something like that if he made C64         music. This SID was finally not released for the diskmag but         in 2014 @ÁROK Party SID compo, placed #3." (NP)

I picked up an unfinished         1994 worktune that I originally created for the Geister game         project and started to expand/refine it. I did not have to start         from the scratch so this SID was ready much sooner than others         I released around that time." (NP)         1994 workfile from the Geister pack as number $0D

TITLE: Crankshaft Pulley
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: GT2.75 "During Vincenzo's C64GTC I realised how magnificent         centerpiece GoatTracker2 is. It sounds good and also so many         trackers can load and read its workfiles. So, if you learn         of how to use GoatTracker2, you can inject the data into         SID-Wizard, NinjaTracker or SID-Factory so that way         you can use various music driver codes. It is handy when you         make something for a raster-hungry demo and convert the tune to         NinjaTracker. About the title: my car visited the mechanic         shop during the time and the guy there said things like         crankshaft pulley, rollbar, flywheel or exhaust manifold." (NP)

Programming manually melody content of this depth would be         quite a mindfuck. For me it took days before SID-Wizard. In some         cases, a week perhaps." (NP)

TITLE: Experiment: Zeta

TITLE: Get to the End
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: SW1.4 + SW1.7 "This is the sibling of the other gameproject that I         made for AVATAR because it had the very same workflow. I turned on         my synth and started playing. I created a 3-channel session file         in Reaper studio software with all the subtunes included then I         converted the whole pack with Hermit's SWMconvert.exe, created         instruments, adjusted sounds, packed exported files and so on.         I wanted to use SIDwizard 1.7 because of its nice advanced         functions but it turned out that it supports 6 subtunes only and I         needed a couple more so I used the older SW1.4 for the ingame tunes         instead because it can handle 16 subs. STILENTRY: COMMENT: SW1.4 "It was one of the most challenging tasks I've ever done on         many sides. I had to keep         in mind from recordnig the first MIDI note that only a couple of         blocks are allowed per subtune because of the memory limit. TITLE: Lilac and Gooseberries
AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Végtelen vidék [from album Sárkányfejezet] ARTIST: Diabolus in MusicaCOMMENT: SW1.8 "That is where 20 minutes can bring you with SID-Wizard.         I wanted to do something for the final round of C64 Grand Tour         challenge that no other tracker can do so I recorded a short         tune with an Arturia Keylab49 keyboard in Reaper, quantised         and arranged channels for a better conversion, exported a         3-channel MIDI file, ran swmconvert.exe on it and set the         sounds and some other stuff. The music data is not touched so         virtually it is me playing the keyboard. SID-Wizard is a         beast of workflow. The title refers to Yennefer from Witcher         books, also my childhood as our garden was full of lilac and         gooseberries. By today, due to climate change they all gone         around my area so that fragrance and memories of the taste         also remind me of good people who gone and it completely rips         my heart out. After those flashbacks I can't find my way for         days. Anyway, this tune is included on Diabouls in Musica LP         with lyrics and acoustic guitars. Coupled with deep lyrics         I always have to focus to the extreme to not to collapse mentally         during live shows when we perform this song called 'Végtelen         vidék' or 'Infinite Landscape' as it is about letting it go and         saying goodbye forever inevitably." (NP)

AUTHOR: Péter Nagy-Miklós (NecroPolo)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Ecce Homo [from Sárkányfejezet] ARTIST: Diabolus in MusicaCOMMENT: GT2.7 "This is an older worktune that I composed on guitar around         2000 or so. It did not fit any of my bands so it rested in the box.         My 'entry composition' for Avatar was a game tunes and FX pack. The         ingame tune needed to be slow-flow and relaxed so I dusted off this         one. Some time later I re-created it with Goat Tracker2 and expanded         it to 3-channels (the gametune is 2-channels) and added a second         part including heavy riffs. It wanted to release it at         Revision 2012 but I missed the deadline as we arrived right after         the oldschool music compo. So, it became released a little later at         Flashback 2012. Then, a massive leap to 2022 where I showed music         pieces for the members of my off-scene project Diabolus in musica.         Finally, this tune ended up to be a supermassive final track for         the band's 2023 album "Sárkányfejezet", titled 'Ecce Homo'. (NP)

TITLE: Bach's Domain
AUTHOR: Oliver Klee (Odi)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!.         Inspired by J.S.Bach again, I composed this piece as another magsound         for 'Genetic Dreams' by Trinomic Boozeline. Willy/Presence favored         this piece a lot (he himself liking Bach, too). I chose the name with         a sidelook to Sascha's piece 'Drax' Domain'. This piece consists of a         few different parts which I just lined up one after another, as I was         unable to come up with some interludes." (OK)

TITLE: Baroque Parting
AUTHOR: Oliver Klee (Odi)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This tunes had been composed with the full player in mind (an loaded         into the editor). That player uses a slight de-tuning for voice #2 and         #3 in order to achieve a fuller sound. In addition, the instruments         make use of pulse width modification.         For the 'zero page version' of this piece, I had cut down the player         to almost nothing in order to get a real short file with as little         raster time as possible. During that step, I removed the routine for         the pulse modification and increased the detuning of voice #2 and #3         instead, resulting in a slightly different (and slightly less nice)         sound." (OK)

TITLE: Baroque Parting (Zero Page)
AUTHOR: Oliver Klee (Odi)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!.         I wrote this piece to express my feelings about a freshly broken         relationship with my (former, sigh) girlfriend. As we just had         analyzed fugues in music class, I wrote a fugue (in c-minor) as well.         There is a zeropage version of this tune that saves even more         rastertime and memory." (OK)

TITLE: Lords of Synthesis
AUTHOR: Oliver Klee (Odi)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Done with my first own music player.         Having read about the great features of Soundmonitor, I got fed up         with the limits of The Music System (TMS) and the music commands from         BASIC V7.0. So I wrote my own soundplayer. That thing ate memory and         rastertime like I drink tea and used a notation similar to the BASIC         commands. But -- it worked and had cool *filters*! I planned to use it         in a Snake-like game I was coding (Crowding Crawlers), but the game         made heavy use of raster interrupts and color effects and thus would         not work with the music (rastertime ranging from $03 to $80 or so...).         I never finished the game anyway. But my trumpet teacher liked the         tune _very_ much! =:-> " (OK)

TITLE: Melt Your Brain
AUTHOR: Oliver Klee (Odi)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Piano Sonata in C (KV 545) (0:00-0:06) ARTIST: Wolfgang Amadeus MozartCOMMENT: "Done with the Cyberlogic Sound Studio... made by me and Sascha/MDG!.         A 4-time techno tune (my best one of this kind so far) which I wrote         together with a good friend of mine, Ingo Meyer. While we were         composing, the speaker box fell off the shelf due to one extremely         loud bass-kick (no kidding!). This piece contributed to the music         competition at the Data-Live '93 in Dessau, winning the 2nd place.         Possibly it would have made the 1st if they had had good big speakers         instead of that tiny thing in their video beamer! =:-( " (OK)         Also used in the game "Orb", (C) 1994 Magic Disk 64/CP Verlag.

TITLE: -19 (Sonic)
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I consider this tune my final breakthrough to the world of good SID         music. The sound is the best I could squeeze out of the Sound         Monitor. Rocks! Only the filtered lead sound at 1:31 doesn't sound in         Sidplay as it's supposed to." (KH)

TITLE: -1 (Omega)
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This tune marks the beginning of a new era of my personal development         as a musician. Until then I had only desperately struggled to get         familiar with the Sound Monitor and its features, and now I actually         started USING them. Originally I only gave the tunes numbers instead         of names, but now, about 20 years later, I felt like it was time to         also add some names." (KH)

TITLE: -20 (Leapfrog)
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "After I had been very content with the tune -19, I lost my         orientation a little. I wanted to try something new, but it became         too bouncy and light-weight, not the way I wanted it to sound like."         (KH)

TITLE: -21 (Xenon)
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "After I had been very content with the tune -19, I lost my         orientation a little. I wanted to try something new, but it became         too bouncy and light-weight, not the way I wanted it to sound like."         (KH)

Especially the         grave part starting at 3:09 isn't as powerful as I wanted it to be."         (KH)

He believed me. ;-) This is my earliest tune         I'm really proud of." (KH)

TITLE: Flyguy
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This tune paints the flight of an Air Force jet, with start, flight         (with stormy weather and clouds inbetween), and finally the landing.         Lead sound starting at 1:54 inspired by Fred Gray's Mutants. Some of         the arpeggios and noise waveforms inspired by Martin Walker's         Armalyte." (KH)

TITLE: Grave
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the SID I'm most proud of. The tune was also recorded later         as "Patty, Kim & Gunnar" with keyboards and vocals and had the title         "Just Good Friends". It was "covered" in 1996 by Dieter Bohlen, who         we had sent a demo tape to, and released in 1996 as Blue System's         single "Only With You" and on his album "Body To Body". Of course I         was neither asked for permission nor given a profit sharing. The         single went #58 on the German charts." (KH)

TITLE: Kirchenlied
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Just a small sound study." (KH)

TITLE: K.I.M.
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I wrote this as a love song for a girl named Kim, at least I thought         so. She of course never listened to it, as she didn't want to have         anything to do with a freaky C64 nerd like me. Weeks later I found         out that the girl's name wasn't Kim at all, but I didn't change the         title of this tune to her real name. Mind the funny ping-pong sound         starting at 3:09! ;-)" (KH)

TITLE: La Serenada
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "With this elaborate composition, I ran out of memory very quickly. At         1:41-1:45 I frivolously used a "forbidden" memory part, so the music         data is overwritten during the initialization of the tune's playback         by the drums samples. Bummer! Tune inspired by Rondo Veneziano." (KH)

TITLE: Live as Friends
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The samples sound quite muddy in this one, probably bc the filter in         the bass sound interferes with them. Bummer!" (KH)

TITLE: Medusa
AUTHOR: Kim Homann (omoroca)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "My first tune with digidrums, which I had ripped from the game         "Danger Freak". This tune marks a turning-point in my personal         development as a musician, putting the focus more on harmonies and         elaborate arpeggios than trying to produce a "cool sound". From this         tune on, I also made myself a strict rule that I FIRST finish         composing the tune on my piano or my Casio keyboard and THEN switch         the C128 on and start with the data input. In order to reflect this,         I also started to give the tunes names instead of numbers again." (KH)

AUTHOR: Reyn Ouwehand
STILENTRY: (#3)   NAME: Intro TuneCOMMENT: The tune falls out of synch at around 4:50, which is when the tune         should loop. However, this is due to the music data in the game         behaving exactly the same way. You would never get to hear this part         of the tune in the game, as the intro would finish and load the first         level before the music got to that point.         "I guess I had some time pressure... TITLE: First
AUTHOR: Jason Page
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "In July 2015, I had surgery, which resulted me in being off work for about 3         months. So, I had some time spare! So, I started writing SID music again for         fun. My first release (FIRST) is very much a 'standard' SID. It has the same         instruments and structure as I was writing and hearing in 1990." (JP)

TITLE: Forth
AUTHOR: Jason Page
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I decided that if I could make the percussion sounds more 'realistic', then I'd         effectively have a synth and a drum machine. For too long, people seem to have         used the same techniques for creating percussion sounds (since Maniacs of         Noise...). I think that a lot of people stopped pushing the SID, and the music         (although great) seemed to be stuck in a rut. I knew FORTH was on the right         track, as some people thought it was fake (using samples / multiple SID's) which         made me happy! It was here that I also tested my theories for some of my         percussion sounds. The hi hats and clap sounds were what I hoped would raise my         SID's to a new level. The hi hats especially, as these really changed the overall         sound of the SID. Most SID's don't have those high frequencies. And the clap, it         sounded like a real drum machine. So again, helped change the perceptions of a         lot of listeners regarding the pushing of SID boundaries." (JP)

TITLE: Sanxion Remix
AUTHOR: Jason Page
STILENTRY: TITLE: Thalamusik [from the game Sanxion] ARTIST: Rob HubbardCOMMENT: "This was another experiment, where I wanted to see if I could remix an existing         (and brilliant) SID tune, but only using a SID. I've heard (and made) a number of         remixes on Remix64, but wanted to attempt to do the same and hopefully be better         than a lot of those, but with nothing but a SID.         This was far more difficult to do than Turrican! I initially converted the whole         of Sanxion to SidTracker64. So, all of the patterns and instruments. So at this         point, I had a version of the track that ran on ST64 in 4x speed (something I've         been doing since Forth. It's how I can get the definition on the clap and         snare...). Only at that point could I start remixing. I didn't want to completely         destroy the feeling of the original, but I wanted to change it enough to make it         worthwhile remixing. It was difficult to gauge what I could do to keep that         balance. Also, the whole track is basically based around ringmod and sync         instruments. What this means is that the sound of, say, the lead instrument, is         effected by another instrument. So, if I modify one instrument for the remix, it         could easily mess up another completely. Likewise, even when porting to ST64, if         an instrument wasn't created exactly as the original, or if I used the wrong         note, it could make the whole thing sound wrong.         But, it seems that a lot of people like the result. I knew it would be down to         personal taste, as the original track is so iconic. I knew some just wouldn't         like it. I can live with that." (JP)

TITLE: Turrican Amiga Port
AUTHOR: Jason Page
STILENTRY: TITLE: Turrican intro music [from the Amiga game] ARTIST: Chris HülsbeckCOMMENT: "For Hybris (which I released before Turrican), I worked out how to reduce         channels but keep the quality. So, I kind of knew that I could get the Amiga's 4         channels down to 3 for Turrican. My main goal here was to write a track that         didn't use ARP's (those instruments where it quickly changes between notes to         create a chord effect). The Amiga version didn't use them, and I felt that if I         had to resort to using them in the port, then I would have failed. It would have         just sounded like a C64 version of an Amiga track. I wanted it to sound just like         the Amiga track, if not better!         It only took 2 days or so to write. The main problem was trying to get the chords         to work, without them cutting out the melody line and so on. It all comes down to         basically tricking the listener. I could remove one voice for another, and as         long as it wasn't *that* noticeable, I could get away with it. Kind of similar to         how MP3's work, by only storing the information that the user can hear, I guess."         (JP)

TITLE: Access Denied (intro)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was done very quick & dirty, if I remember right I've had only         3-4 hours time to compose this track in our new developed and         finished Reflex-Tracker, a 2 channel sampletracker. Access Denied         sample spoken by me. The bass-drumm split was make with an Amiga 500         and converted to my C64. Later in version v1.1 of Reflex-Tracker the         user could do this without directly in the trakker. Funny: most of         the time in this song I use only one digichannel, after release I         created a remix which prooves the ability of Reflex-Tracker a little         bit better. After winning the C64 democompo at THE PARTY'94 in         Denmark, most of the people thought our group name is 'Access Denied'         but it was 'Reflex' instead ;)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Access Denied (remix)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the remix of Access_Denied_intro.sid where I show some of the         features of Reflex-Tracker: 2 channels of digi-sounds, faked third         voice (drum and snare which are rendered in the bassvoice), volume,         echoeffects and flanger. All samples by me, except the "ho ho" which         I have sampled from the german rap song 'Edelweiß'." (PVCF)

TITLE: Africa Corps
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Interesting fact: it's a 2 channel digi music but not a         Reflex-Tracker tune. It's a routine which allows you theoretical add         3 SID voices. The music editor is named 'Perfect Sound 3.2'.         Unfortunately the 2 digi voices have always the speed (and pitch) of         the first digi voice and if you really use both voices the SID         channels were nearly destroyed and the CPU was down...         We used this track in the note file of our (Reflex) first trackmo         'Cafe Odd'. Later it became a very nice practice for us to use always         a very special notefile-soundroutine for our trackmos.         All (!) samples was sampled with my Phillips-Workman!!         Sample-software by Zork and TTS! Sampler by Zork's Brother." (PVCF)

TITLE: Axel F
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Axel F [from the movie Beverly Hills Cop] ARTIST: Harold FaltermeyerCOMMENT: "My second doublespeed tune. After all the other conversions of this         great song I thought it was a good idea not only to use the original         melody. The great mood with the sfx and sounds should even be copied.         At 2:01 I started to remix the song with some special drums and         clave sticks." (PVCF)

TITLE: Black Crystall
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "If you are using a old SID chip or emulation you will probably not         hear too much from the melody line, the 6581 doesn't know the used         $31 waveform. Sorry for that. Doesn't know much about this song, its         15 years ago and this song was only made just 4 fun and to learn...         I never planned to release this song (and during composing this I         even didn't have the ability to do this^^)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Bladeswede
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: TITLE: px.bladeswede remix! [from the Amiga game Project-X] ARTIST: Allister BrimbleCOMMENT: "I listened to Allister Brimble's great song on Amiga and decided that         this song has to be remixed to the C64. Unfortunately I don't have         the needed amount of channels so I used a big bunch of arpeggio-lead         & bass-splits. The patterns looks like a exploded memorydump, it was         very hard to compose this with a durationeditor (DMC4.x). I really         forced the lead melody between the arpeggios. The music got used in         Access Denied trackmo-notefile with a raytraced animation and a         layered scroller. Regarding our tradition to use some special in our         trackmo-notefiles I tried a faked 4 speed tune, that means: normal         doublespeed routine and additionally I called the sidroutine 2 times         (without the filterroutine), that gives: 4speed wave and 2speed         filter." (PVCF)

TITLE: Brainbeat 3 Introrap
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Again a Reflex-Tracker song, the rap and the beats are realtime         mixed. Rapped by myself ;) The string was ripped from Georg Brandt's         Paranoia_Complex.sid, Tune #1, thanks to Georg! As I've made this tune         I thought it would be a revolution, the first realtime rap on C64 and         so... but no one, I repeat: no one! cared about ;) Later I composed         a very long CBA&Nightshade hate hip-hop track, (they have stolen and         cracked a game which we have made), but this song was never spread by         our swapper Happymaker. Very sad.)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Breitbandkatze
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor         called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC). Nothing special here, I think I         have composed this tune mustly to show what clear filter sounds are         possible with this routine. It's a single speeder. Unfortunately I         didn't know the trackmo (Breitbandkatze / Reflex) and the demo parts         during composing. You need a new SID chip, or you will miss some         complete channels. It's possible that this tune is the track, which I         would do just for fun with the goal that no voices are listenable on         a old SID chip. But I'm not sure if I realy have done this, its not         very hard to do such things ;) (my intention: all my filtereffects         sounds horrible on a old SID and I thought it was better to show         listeners with old SID nothing than crap) it was the last song which         I did on C64 after 5 years of SID composing. Since 2001 and now         (2008) I rarely compose SID tunes with QuadraSID, one or two times per         year. Some of this tracks you can download from my website as mp3         (www.reflex-studio.com)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Café Odd
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The first trackmo of our group Reflex which was released at THE PARTY         '93. The first trackmo with a doublespeed music 8) This was the first         music of me on C64 which was really released AND spreaded ;) This         trackmo also have two 2 channel digiparts! The first one is in the         notefile, listen to Africa_Corps.sid and read the STIL comments!         The second one is the first version of our 2 years later released         Reflex-Tracker. The Cafe_Odd_end.sid digi music was composed in pure         assembler." (PVCF)(#1)COMMENT: 6581 version.(#2)COMMENT: 8580 version.

TITLE: Café Odd (end)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is the first music which was done in the Reflex-Tracker engine,         without editor. 8) I "composed" this track live at THE PARTY'93 in         Denmark, in assembler... I typed the pattern and notes with Action         Replay monitor in the memory. It was a very funny time, with hardcore         party in the sleeping hall and so on 8)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Centric
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I've spent very long time for the whole project, I think something         about 6-9 months (besides graduation diploma and some rfx-trackmos).         as the game was finished and the music was put in and I played it,         I noticed: "shit, I've made the first ingame musics very very long,         2-5 minutes each and the players died after some seconds of playing!"         That was a very harsh lesson. Oh, and the game sold horrible...         Later I composed most of the following songs a little bit shorter."         (PVCF)(#1)COMMENT: "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor         called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC)." (PVCF)(#2)COMMENT: "This was the menu tune" (PVCF)(#3)COMMENT: "Loader tune" (PVCF)(#4)COMMENT: "ingame1, huh, about every 30 seconds a totally different style."         (PVCF)(#5)COMMENT: "ingame2, if you like techno on C64 this song is possible for you"         (PVCF)(#6)COMMENT: "nice ringmodulation at the beginning, it was only a loader tune."         (PVCF)(#7)  TITLE: Danger Freak, Tune #1 ARTIST: Chris HülsbeckCOMMENT: "ingame3, I tried to copy the original melody and soundset from         'Danger Freak/Chris Hülsbeck'. Just 4 fun :)" (PVCF)(#8)COMMENT: "ingame4, too long, too many styles, too much work..." (PVCF)(#9)COMMENT: "Only a loadertune" (PVCF)(#10)COMMENT: "ingame5, a multispeed song, the original title is         'dance of the robot', one of my favourite songs :)" (PVCF)(#11)  TITLE: Scapelands ARTIST: Kai Walter (PVCF)COMMENT: "ingame6, a very nice remix of Scapelands.sid, just after the first         30 seconds of boreness, which was released in Access Denied trackmo.         I also put in some Martin Galway like athmosphere, listen from         1:30 for this." (PVCF)

TITLE: Centric (end sequence)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The SID music and the digisequence was composed with two different         routines: 3sid voices in DMC4.x and after finishing I have loaded         it in Polonus' DigiTracker and added the samplesequences. Very         funny way to compose: if you changed a sample, for example after         2 min in songlength, you have to start the song from begin to check         if it works in minute two. I was very masochistic those days.         Polonus did NOT include a fast forward routine, so later I added         one in his editor." (PVCF)

TITLE: Centric (trackmo)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The trackmo Centric/Reflex of our gamesection 'Cyance' won a C64/Amiga         democompetition at a multiplatform party in Berlin in 1996, IIRC. We         decided to give up the trackmo spontaneously, but it was a big success         :) To tell the truth: I don't like this song very much, especially the         total uninspired first minute is horrible. It's a doublespeed song.         This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor         called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC)." (PVCF)

TITLE: Dresden Party'95 II
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This song was composed live on a local computerparty. I would say it         was funny, but on other had: how funny is a party where you sit down         and work on a C64 and there is only one of this machine running and         other people (Ron Grahnert aka Odysseus) are even bored and tried to         get his hands on the keyboard? So we found a compromise and worked         10 min each on DMC :) That's the result!         Ah, one interesting thing: it's a special more and halfspeed-mix. One         channel (arpeggio channel) is halfspeeded and the other 2 channels         are massive multispeeded (did I mention that it was very bored at this         party ? ;) For exact details about the routine you can simply         watch the partydemo which was released together with BrainBeat 4,         called Party Dresden 95. If you find out that it sounds different in         the demo; that's right. However the tune in HVSC sounds as I've         intended it to sound :) The swinging logo have destroyed the         multispeed routine." (PVCF)

TITLE: Dr. Nabla
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Look Who's Talking [from Look Who's Talking] ARTIST: Dr. AlbanCOMMENT: "Yeah, a 5-speed tune, IIRC. The drumtable was longer than my arm ;)         Just composed for fun. it sounds a little disharmonic at begin, that's         caused by Brian/Graffity, who didn't implement the right frequency         table in his DMCs. From DMC4 I used a own table, which         KB/TOM/farbrausch has edited. From 2:30 min there are very nice         remixes and soundeffects which are inspired by the samples from Bad         Cat by Chris Hülsbeck  8)" (PVCF)

TITLE: The Ende
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Made in GMC, the predecessor of the great DMC. One of my first songs         in a duration editor, right after 7 months of composing in         Soundmonitor. For more details look at comments for Game_Over.sid.         This song got never released, its a HVSC first release." (PVCF)

TITLE: execute_overdrive_intro
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Centric, Tune #3 ARTIST: Kai Walter (PVCF)COMMENT: "I was very surprised in 2004 as I heard this track in a new Smash         Designs trackmo. Hm, I stopped composing on C64 in 1997 and in 2004         there appears a new song... what happened? After analyzing the chords         and melodies it was clear: it must be a working track, maybe a loader         tune for Centric. AEG, which is the lead programmer of Smash Designs,         has the permission (since 1995) to use all PVCF-C64 songs on all C64         productions and so he did :) I'm not sure, but I think he used more         of my musics in his trackmos than we could in Reflex ;) Ah, AEG, if         you care (and if you read this) : I've really planned in 1992(?)         (after your first demo (bei nebenwirkungen essen sie die         packungsbeilage...)) to ask you if I could join Smash Designs, no         joke! But in those times my musics were so bad that I waited and then         I got an offer from Reflex." (PVCF)

TITLE: Fast Shit (Insider 3.2)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Uh, that name was harshly criticised by Happymaker which was         responsible for our mag 'Insider'. I don't know why I called it         Fast Shit, but it was very important for me... ;)         Nice doublespeed tune, made in DMC3.x." (PVCF)

TITLE: For Guilty
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Bad story: to become famous I thought I compose some tunes for other         groups, so they spread my musics with their demos/mags. I spent a         lot of time for this tune. After 2 years or so a guy from Guilty         met my at a party and told me something like "I'm so so sorry, but         we haven't released your track, because blabla", I was very pissed off.         So in fact it's a HVSC release." (PVCF)

TITLE: For Ingenious Brain 5
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Same like For_Guilty.sid, to become famous I thought I compose some         tunes for other groups, so that they spread my musics whith their         demos/mags. So I spent a lot of time for this tune. I don't know if         I really sent it to the mag Ingenious Brain, but if I did or not, the         song was never released there. I put it later in one of my         soundcollections 'Brainbeat'. After 1:40 it changes to a new song..."         (PVCF)

TITLE: For Insider 02
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "One of my earlier works, every 30 seconds a complete different theme         :/  Later I used part 2:50-3:00 as the base for Nova 2, track #7         (The scratch effect, I think)" (PVCF)

TITLE: Geometric 2
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: (#1)COMMENT: "The task: compose a absolut High Quality techno song for the intro of         our AFLI game :) I think its my best techno song on C64, it's a         doublespeeder which really forces the 8580 to its limits. The ingame         songs are simple singlespeeders, but I've spent much time in editing         filter LFOs to get those clear and hard sounds on DMC3. IIRC the coder         (Quiss) gave the tester of a german C64 mag called "64'er" a call and         asked him to use a new SID chip for the review of the game. I got 10         of 10 points for the music :) Sadly only one of the 2 ingame tracks         were used. Some memory problems... The same sh*t like nowadays on         NintendoDS :(" (PVCF)(#3)COMMENT: "I really love the echo-arpeggios after 1:33 and the echo effect in         the flute lead. It's only one channel, I added the echo-effect with         a simple trick: I repeated the last two notes with very low volume."         (PVCF)

TITLE: Giana 2
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Very funny story why I created this song: if you look carefully in         this directory you will find a song called "Axel_F" which I adapted         from Harold Faltermeyer. I found out, if I play the original Beverly         Hills Cop chords from Axel F in the other direction OR simultaneously         it's exact(!) the same like "The Great Giana Sisters, Tune #5".         To answer all other game related questions: NO!  :)         It was NOT a Giana/Mario-clone. It was NOT released. I have NO copy         (only one level was finished and playable, ask Quiss!) We do NOT have         had a permission to use the name and the sprites of Giana :) The idea:         what do if you get stressed by work / family / girlfriend/... ? What         about a game where you can shoot very brutal? What enemy would you         like to kill to vent your anger? Right! The dinky Giana Sister :p         And what weapon would you like to use to kill Giana? Right! A tank! So         here is the game: you have a tank with a machinegun which drove from         right to left (on your will) and from above it was raining little         Giana Sisters with parachutes. Now you could use your heavy machinegun         and blow them into hell (subtune #6!). If you missed one and landed in         front of you, you could try to drive with your tank chain over Giana :)         then #5 was played. If you only have destroyed the parachute and         little Giana falls & hit the ground #4 was played. #7 if a Giana hits         your tank (and eats some of your health)." (PVCF)(#1)  TITLE: Great Giana Sisters, Tune #5 ARTIST: Chris HülsbeckCOMMENT: "The SID music and the digisequence was composed with two different         routines; DMC3 and Polonus' DigiTracker. Very funny way to compose:         if you changed a sample, for example after 2 min in songlength,         you have to start the song from begin to check if it works in min 2.         I was very masochistic those days. Polonus did NOT include a fast         forward routine, so I added one in his editor.         The samples: for track 1 I used some placeholder voices (bad man,         sumba-he!) just to see if the spoken samples work, after some months         of work on this game and the decision that we do not release the game         I stopped the work and I left the samples like they were. Later I         released the Giana 2 soundpack in Brainbeat 4, SideB." (PVCF)(#2)COMMENT: "Ingame tune. 2 voices only, so we could use the remaining one for the         digi effects." (PVCF)(#3)COMMENT: "Was supposed to be the loadertune and the highscore track." (PVCF)

TITLE: Mathematica (tune 2)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor         called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC). One of my costly and longest LSD         tracks. in this routine I could trigger demoparts with numeric         commands in the soundpattern, Quiss (the programmer of LSD and some         of the trackmoparts in Mathematica) have included a fallback routine         in the demo, that waits 10 sec if the floppydrive of the user is to         slow and a trigger was missed. Unfortunately he forgot to tell me that         the first numeric trigger he was expecting was a "0". But I began the         count with "1" ... so 10 sec failbackpause is in all versions of         mathematica, right before the Doom-part. Funny thing: exact 5.34 min         long was the centerpart, I composed exact 5.34 min :)  but I don't         know about the 10 sec fall back routine, and Quiss didn't tell me...         he simply took notice that the music was too "short", removed the         stop-bytes at the end of the LSD track and was satisfied. Watching         the trackmo first time and live at THE PARTY'95 I was pissed of as         I saw/heard the result: the music wild remixed itself after 5.34         unless the last part was finished. I learned one thing:         (its true up to now, 2008!!) programmers don't have any savvy about         music. Last funny thing: I asked all people around me what they         thought about this crazy and disharmonic music?  All(!) comments         sounded like this: "If PVCF compose like this it has to be like         this" ... aha.. ha ..ha... Funny thing: after the democompetition         the organizers have shown this trackmo again, in this time (1995)         Mathematica was like a revolution on C64 in design & code and I         put in at 1:36 a little irish sounding melody which forced some         people with hooked arms to dance together on tables, I was very         very very proud :p  It's possible that you need a new SID chip to         hear this part, sorry for that. (yes, the trackmo has a         SID chip-selector and detector, but this should be used in an other         trackmo of us, read the STIL comments for         Mathematica_tune_1_6581.sid for more information about this)." (PVCF)

TITLE: Megasweet (6581)
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Uhh, this song taught me a very hard lesson: save your work every         3-5 minutes, ... save !!!!         I worked on Megasweet a whole day and I swear, it was twice as good         as what you can hear now. But after about 8 hours of composing on my         C64 (it was a sunny day, I ought to learn for my A-level examination)         the C64 was freezed (a DMC-crash which occured about once per year).         After that I was so frustrated that I released this truly unfinished         version. Check out the great mp3 conversion from DJ SKITZ. To be         honest I have ripped out the idea for the filtered glide effect in         the main bassline from an Amiga-mod called "Megasweet". I thought         it would be nice to try something similar on C64 for testing purpose.         Then I added the chord, but didn't play it as arpeggio-sound (typical         C64), instead I played it like a triad, very slow and voila - the         base idea of the first real trance/chill techno music on C64 was         born. Now the "work" begun: in DMC4 doesn't exists a filtercommand         in pattern, so I must use different filtered basses and endless         glide-effects in bassline. It's not much fun to work like this." (PVCF)

TITLE: Radio Napalm
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was made for and released in the trackmo 'Radio Napalm' of our         group 'Reflex', which has won a party, but I can't remember which.         [It won the X'95 demo competition held in Utrecht, Netherlands]         Quiss told me it was shown with a old SID chip 6581 and the music         wasn't that what it should be supposed to, but the crowd was so         impressed by the trackmo that the applause during the whole demo         was even louder than the sound equipement. So the old SID wasn't         that much of a problem :)         It's a DMC music and I hate it for the 16 slots instrument         limitation, you can hear it: the filter doesn't sweep smooth at the         first part, they are like triggered in a mod file. :( Later I         released this song in one of our Brainbeat music collections, but         I forgot to relocate the song, so every one could load the tune         directly in his DMC. The result: some very bad remixes (which uses         this horrible filter off-set soundsystem). The party [the demo was         released on] had a limitation in length of demos: 5 minutes. So first         I composed the music as a 5 minutes track. Unfortunately Quiss (the         coder of the trackmo) didn't get enough parts in time to fill up         the 5 minutes complete. We first have planned to show during the         whole demo a backward timer which runs from 5 min to 0 with the         comment "We hate timelimits!!!". After Quiss told me the lack of a         needed last part I shortened the music drastically. I have done this         track on a new SID chip, KB/TOM (now farbrausch) later converted         this song for the old SID chip and released a "old SID chip" version         of the trackmo." (PVCF)

TITLE: Reflection
AUTHOR: Kai Walter (PVCF)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is one of the few songs which I have made in our own SID-editor         called LSD (Low Sound Dealer, IIRC). Again I got the whole finished         trackmo 'Reflection' from Quiss and I could compose the music right         fitting to the parts. It's an unusual multispeed setup: the first         channel is singlespeed, the second double and the third something         around 4-6, don't know anymore. It was only possible with our new NMI         timer trackmosystem, no dull rastertime ;). Hehe, no one have beat         this, I think 8) The next step should be a trackmo with multispeed         LSD music and a one channeled digiroutine. LSD was prepared for this,         but Quiss and I haven't found the time to manage a new trackmo and         complete the LSD composer due to our gamedeveloping ambitions on PC.         I don't know exactly at which party we released this trackmo, but         it could be THE PARTY 95 together with Mathematica, but I'm not         sure as mentioned." (PVCF)         [The demo Reflection was released at the Convention 1996]

AUTHOR: Jan D. Arent Harries (rambones)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "One of my personal favourites, despite the fact that I used it in an         apology demo to Zetrex 2005. My good friends Wizz & Kaze demanded me         to do this demo in order to stop the war. To compensate for my loss of         face, I filled the screen with my name in sprites, dancing around so         that you only would remember 2 things after having seen the demo: the         music and the name RAMBONES. :) What a hoax, Kaze got his software         from me, and me and TSN visited Wizz every weekend. There's some         really nice filter in this one, so try a C64." (JH)

AUTHOR: Jan D. Arent Harries (rambones)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "That's exactly what my emotions were as I used this tune in my last         demo, on the last screen. It was the Dexion-party in 1988. I had         released 'Apolloguys' the same day, and I had bought my Amiga 500 only         2 weeks before coming to this party. The first screen featured 'Like         Galway', and me writing a lot of text about who and what 'Rambones'         was. The middle screen was the 'Amiga Noid' screen, with a small         picture of an Amiga, and a scroll telling that TST would soon rule it.         The last one, with this music, was a 10 point list of things about the         C64 that bored the hell out of me. Things like colorbars, sprites         moving in sinus, Hubbard alike drums/routines, all with the same sound         and generally everything that was in at that time. For me it was sad         to see a large variety of composers using more or less the same         routine, leaving the music in a grey state. I admire the sound of Fred         Gray, Martin Galway, Rob Hubbard, David Whittaker, Ben Daglish and         Antony Crowther, and any other programmer that built it all up from         scratch." (JH)

TITLE: Oceanic
AUTHOR: Jan D. Arent Harries (rambones)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This needs filter! (C64)... As I saw that Jonathan Dunn continued to         make music for Ocean, I thought that maybe I had a chance also, so I         sent this tune to the company. I never got a reply. :) well, I didn't         really care anyway because I now was using Soundtracker every day, all         day long. My newfound inspiration: SLL .. :) After having made my         first few Soundtracker-modules, I sent a demo with some musics and a         picture to Hewson. They replied: your music is quite good, but we         cannot accept you as a graphics-artist, the picture lacks all kind of         inspiration. Arrrghh.... Their music in their games sucked bigtime         back then... This is the last tune that I made in 1988." (JH)

TITLE: Ode to Banana (V1)
AUTHOR: Jan D. Arent Harries (rambones)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Everybody old enough knows the 'Ode To Martin' by MC/Dutch USA-Team.         One of my good contacts, and a very musical one to was Banana/The         Electronic Knights. He had already made more than 30 tunes when I         first laid my hands on Soundmon. I didn't know at all how to use this         program, but I could hear from Chris' and Banana's music that it         definately was the way to go. So I asked Banana for some help. He sent         me about 10 handwritten pages, how to type in this bass and use         the program. So, it was my FIRST tune ever!" (JH)

Of course, another 'Ode to...' :) I kinda         like this, as did he, but there's hardly any bass in it, because I try         (again) to make some drums.,, One more thing: the sounds were made by         Laxity. :)" (JH)

TITLE: Resolute
AUTHOR: Jan D. Arent Harries (rambones)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "We are in the final chapter of my C64 days. I was composing / drawing         / programming / writing, all alone on my final demo: Zound Muzak #4.         I had just learned FLD, 8-9 months after everybody else, but at least         I didn't just rip it. I started on several tunes at the same time, to         try and get them all to sound as they came from one whole, like Mike         Oldfield does. This was the first one, but I never finished ZM4, I was         too bored after all." (JH)(#1)   NAME: RevolutionCOMMENT: Previously this tune was only playing a subset of the whole song,         the final version was forgotten and found out in 2023 after 35 years.(#2)   NAME: ResoluteCOMMENT: The version previously available, played at the intended speed.

I made it at a visit to         one of my friends, trying to teach him about using Soundmon. It was         made in about half an hour, then I had to go on to another friend.         I was so busy, driving around on my moped, dumping demos/games, and         then on to the next. Finally, every evening, I would end up at TSN's         place, and our democoding-session could begin, and last until it was         time to go to school... :)" (JH)

STILENTRY: TITLE: Snik ARTIST: Jeroen SoedeCOMMENT: The original is /MUSICIANS/S/SoedeSoft/Soede_Jeroen/Snik.sid,         but before that, it was named Tusker_Intro.sid and placed in         /DEMOS/UNKNOWN.         "This was a desperate attempt of doing a cover of the Tusker_Intro         tune, as I wanted to use it in a demo. But the version I had of it was         bugged, and fell out of synch when looping. This isn't ANYTHING close         to the original version, but... the reason why this one didn't get a         name, is that I at the time didn't know where the tune came from or         who made it." (TRS)

TITLE: Love Sees No Color
AUTHOR: Tom Roger Skauen (Sidewinder)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Living on Video [from Living on Video] ARTIST: Trans-XCOMMENT: "Many people may wonder why this tune is named "Love Sees No Color"         when the tune's name infact is "Living On Video". Well, this is due to         the fact I didn't know the tune's name... just what it sounded like,         and TDS / Fluid told me that the name WAS "Love Sees No Color", and I         ofcourse trusted him. Shouldn't have done that ;)" (TRS)         There exists an alternate version of U96's Love Sees No Colour called         Version 2 (to be found on the Maxi Single CD) which is in fact a         cover version of Trans-X's Living On Video. Hope this solves the         mystery (info from Stefan 'Pohli' Pohlmann).

TITLE: Skilles Johanne
AUTHOR: Tom Roger Skauen (Sidewinder)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Skilles Johanne ARTIST: SputnikCOMMENT: "This is a cover of a tune by a Norwegian artist called Sputnik. He is         a truck-driver, and sings in his spare-time. And he's actually not         singing 100% clean, and YET he's been releasing HEAPS of albums.         Mostly bought by really old people. The title translated to English,         would be something like "Divorcing Johanne". And not surprisingly, the         tune is about a man who wants to get divorced ;) I do NOT listen to         such music, the inspiration came from a techno-version of this made on         Amiga back in 94 I think. :)" (TRS)

TITLE: Acid Stomach
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes (Nutt '67)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Called 'Acid Stomach' because the sound at the every fourth bar         sounds a bit like someone vomiting... well, that's what I thought,         anyway. Again, not exactly what you'd call 'a nice tune' but I was         just seeing what you could do with a few basic sequences by mixing and         transposing them. At the time I didn't really like 'acid' music, I was         more likely to listen to John Cage or Pierre Henry, so I wasn't really         sure how to write it. SoedeSoft editor again. Horrible drums again,         the snare being a bit like the one in 'Thalamusic'." (BH)

TITLE: Feedback Experiment
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes (Nutt '67)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This tune does exactly what it says on the box, basically trying to         get a ring-mod effect that sounded like an electric guitar being left         leaning on a Marshall amplifier turned up to 11. I was fairly pleased         with the result, it sounds quite uncomfortable on headphones. The tune         was written on a SoedeSoft editor, which explains the rather fuzzy         triggering and messy drum sounds, but gliding and filter control was         much more versatile than anything else around at the time, I felt, and         you could sustain notes for about 5 hours. The tune was not written         especially for the "Acid At The PC Show" demo, having being composed         around 8 weeks earlier, but Shane (coder) wanted to use them." (BH)

TITLE: Fly by Night
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes (Nutt '67)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Fly By Night ARTIST: Paul HardcastleCOMMENT: "Oh dear! Let's face it, Neil Baldwin did the best C64 version of this         ever, and it was foolish to try and emulate it... This was done on         SoedeSoft (I think) at 5am on the Sunday morning of the 1989 PC Show         in London (hence the demo title). Has a long ending after a drum solo         that John Bonham would probably laugh at. I also did a version of this         tune in Ubiks Music in 1988, which was even worse. I hope that's never         found!" (BH)

TITLE: Galway Remix
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes
STILENTRY: TITLE: Ocean Loader 1 ARTIST: Martin GalwayCOMMENT: "Just done to test out the System 6581 editor, which I'd just got -         and this is one of my very favourite C64 tunes ever. It was never         meant to be released but we ended up sticking in on an SG demo disk         anyway. Note that one of the arpeggios is a bit wonky, and I couldn't         be bothered to do the start of the piece, but I felt that it was a         pretty good sound-a-like." (BH)

TITLE: The Greed Monster
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Another day, another pointless budget game. Yogi Bear deserved         better! I can't remember if I composed the tune or if it was a         conversion of some Atari ST music, written by some bloke who's name I         can't remember. We used to do a few conversions back then. These were         great fun to do. The software company would sent Gerard Gourley a copy         of the original music, usually recorded on a cassette recorder sitting         by the TV. He'd then play the tune down the telephone to me, and I'd         record it on another cassette from the telephone's earpiece. The         resulting hi-fidelity master recording would then be my basis. I         usually had to guess at the basslines, as they'd become totally         inaudible on the tape. Then I'd U-U the result back to Gerard within 2         hours, and if I was lucky I'd get £100 about 6 months later after the         'middle man' had taken his bit. Or half that if the tune was for         Ocean." (BH)

TITLE: Prison Riot
AUTHOR: Ben Hayes
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Composed for another dodgy budget game, in the old SG editor I think,         which was written by Andy Lumley. I probably had about 12 hours notice         to write this... Zzap reviewed it and called it siren 'music', so they         can't have listened to more than about 10 seconds of it. I quite liked         it at the time, but more for the effects than the rather scrappy lead         lines. Tune #4 was totally different in style, for the hiscore table.         [...] To be honest, music for this sort of game was an afterthought         - and for the money I was getting, I wasn't about to try and write an         epic!" TITLE: Bojojoing
AUTHOR: Otto Järvinen (SounDemoN)
STILENTRY: (#1)COMMENT: "Some people claim that everything imaginable has been done on the C64.         This is true to a certain extent. The typical scenario is indeed that         you come up with something new just to find out that someone else has         done it 10 years ago... But sometimes strange things happen and even         lamers like myself stumble on new stuff. This happened when we were         working on our 4k intro Pico! for Breakpoint this year. I was coding         the music player and tried to create some drum sounds when I         accidentally got some harsh, very distorted sounds. The funny thing         was that I was using the noise waveform and got something that sounded         like a synthesized electric guitar!" (SounDemoN)

TITLE: E-Motion
AUTHOR: Mark Tait
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "E-Motion was my last game for Tiertex. I completely rewrote my music         routine for the C64, so that it used a constant raster/processing, as         a handover to the musician who was replacing me (I was leaving, I         wasn't pushed). :) I don't know if he ever used it." (MT)

TITLE: Human Killing Machine
AUTHOR: Mark Tait
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Human Killing Machine was my attempt to write a soundtrack that         sounded like Martin's Comic Bakery. Depending on which review you         read, it was either pretty good or the worst music anyone had ever         programmed on the C64. :)" (MT)(#1)  TITLE: Comic Bakery, Tune #1 ARTIST: Martin GalwayCOMMENT: The whole music shows a big resemblance to this tune, especially the         bassline and the arpeggios.         "I will freely admit to Rob Hubbard and Martin Galway being my biggest         influences of the time (as far as computer games were concerned), and         I will not deny at all that their music had a certain influence on me.         I truly wish however, that no-one thinks that I was ever copying them.         If any of their sounds or productions in general rubbed off on me, I         can only hope that they thought of me as a fan, and not as a         plagarist." (MT)(#3)COMMENT: Almost the same as /MUSICIANS/T/Tait_Mark/Music_Demo_7.sid, Tune #3.

TITLE: Thunder Blade
AUTHOR: Mark Tait
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Thunder Blades music was produced over night. It was decided that a         demo of a level would be appearing on the cover of Zzap! 64. The         actual C64 game was not written by Tiertex (although the other         versions were), it was a guy called Chris someone. As I remember, he         credited everyone but me!" (MT) (Chris someone = Chris Butler)         "ThunderBlade is another favourite and one I loved doing. We got the         proper arcade machine into the office to play with. The title music         was a little different, no four-to-the-floor, a little more fluty.         Then the in-game music just takes over. [...] the game was pretty         good, and I made the music sound as much like helicopter blades as         possible. I was really pleased with it, and as I recall, ZZap!64         gave it a pretty good score, too." (MT)(#1)  TITLE: Thunder Blade [from the arcade game Thunder Blade] ARTIST: Koichi Namiki (Pretty K.N)

AUTHOR: Stu Taylor
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I had been commissioned by Orpheus Software (ironically the makers of         Electrosound) to code the music for their game Sky Runner. They sent         me a work-in-progress version of the game along with a         sort-of-completed Electrosound composition. They wanted me to         transpose this to a non-Electrosound version and make it my own - what         you hear on here is the end result. Unfortunately the MD of Orpheus at         the time was a complete nightmare to work with - I was young and naive         at the time but this was my first experience, commercially, of trying         to get money out of someone. He just wouldn't pay - kept saying cheque         would be in the post, give it another week or so etc etc....looking at         Sky Runner for the first time ever (on [CSDb.dk]) it looks like the         programmer's deal with Orpheus went pretty sour as well. I see the         game was published by another software house (Cascade?) and the music         had gone back to it's original Electrosound composition - obviously I         had no dealings with Cascade - they probably didn't even know about my         arrangement!!.... About 1 year later, under new management, Orpheus         approached me again asking me to do some more music. OK, I said,         firstly you pay me for Sky Runner and secondly I want the money for         the new music (I think it was an adaption of some board game involving         moving buses around London???) up front - they obliged so there was a         happy ending to this story." (ST)         The original tune can be found in /GAMES/S-Z/Sky_Runner.sid

STILENTRY: COMMENT: This tune was the original prototype for the title theme from Savage.         Jeroen did this first, sampling the Dutch comedian Harry Vermeegen.         'Koud he' was his catchphrase and translated it means 'Cold eh?'.         His most notorious use of this was a Dutch TV programme called 'Pisa'         (filmed from the leaning tower) with Harry saying his 'Koud He?'         catchphrase to everyone that went by. Probe Software then heard the         tune and asked Jeroen if he'd change the samples, and lo and behold it         became the Savage theme.         "Some background info. The 'KOUD HE' sample is from a Dutch comedian         called 'Harry Vermeegen'. It was like a hype saying. I found it a nice         sample to play around with. A spontanious tune I did just 4 fun." (JT)

TITLE: Nighthunter
AUTHOR: Jeroen Tel
STILENTRY: COMMENT: " 'Nighthunter' voice is me. The 'laughing' and the 'Allright!' is ME         and my BROTHER, just before we're about to hit town. That explain the         silly 'BURP!' and 'AJIIRK' too. My brother was pushing me to go with         him, so I asked him to sample some voices real fast. (in this case,         rather silly ones.) This is probably the most 'rushed' music I've ever         made. (which shows somehow). I like many of the ideas in it, but I         just had to meet the deadline. No time for quality checks... just...         PRODUCE and DELIVER. Too bad somehow. It give us a funny compilation         of brainactivity though :O         BTW: If you want to know my brother's name: It's 'Kees Tel' (he's an         awesome composer and musician. He composes almost any imaginable style         of music and plays a LOT of instruments.)" (All comments by JT.)

TITLE: 2nd Debut
AUTHOR: Pawel Ruczko (H.M.Murdock)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "2 years after my last zak I decided to come back to business. So I         asked Klax for an exclusive instrument, which covers sounds from         Future Composer. He did that for me and I've started to compose tunes         once again. Done on 18.11.2001. Tune length 01:16." (PR)

TITLE: 3 Years Ago
AUTHOR: Pawel Ruczko (Murdock)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "The first part of this song was composed before Symphony 2003 party.         After a few months I decided to finish this song and I released it on         the TUM 2003 party. The tune got placed 4th. The title reminds me of         what was happening exactly 3 years ago. I like this tune very much.         Done on 17.12.2003 using Future Composer v4.0. Tune length 02:55."         (PR)

TITLE: 4 Rea
AUTHOR: Pawel Ruczko (H.M.Murdock)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "An exclusive tune done for Rea. A speedy tune in Hardcore mood.         Composed using Data's exclusive instruments on Hardtrack Composer.         Done on 02.12.2001. Tune length 02:06." (PR)

TITLE: Acid Runner Remix
AUTHOR: Pawel Ruczko (V-12)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This is one of 4 remixes which I made back in 1999 under Hardtrack         Composer. Later I've lost 3 of them but "Acid Runner Remix" got         discovered on dusted tape which I've got from my old swapp contact         named Alien. It turned out that he still had the tape which we've been         using for swapping. Tune lenght 1:33." (PR)         Composed in 1999, released in 2015.         Remix of /MUSICIANS/L/Longhair/Drip.sid, contains patterns from         subtunes 3, 6 and 7.

AUTHOR: Pawel Ruczko (H.M.Murdock)

Done on 21.03.2002 using Hardtrack Composer and with         Shapie's exclusive instruments. Tune length 02:40." (PR)

TITLE: Walker's Warbles
AUTHOR: Martin Walker
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Walker's Warbles" was a Martin Walker music demo which came as a free         giveaway with the disk version of "Armalyte" by Thalamus (which MW did         the music for.) Tune #3 is an early version of what would eventually be         used in the game "Dominion" bundled on a Zzap! 64 covertape in 1990,         and tune #4 is an early version of the "Aggressor Theme". The final         version of this (and the one which Revolution uses) is the one on MW's         "Zzap! 64 Music Demo" which appeared on Zzap 64's June 1989 covermount         cassette. (Comment by Warren Pilkington)(#4)COMMENT: This tune was also used in a game called Revolution (written by Simon         Pick). The game was never released, but featured on Commodore Format         magazine's powerpack (tape) number one.

TITLE: AMS Composer
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "I remember doing a little demo for Andy Startin at the time which         had a piano keyboard and also one of the tunes from the Merry         Christmas II demo (before I finished the demo.)  I sent it to him         so he could have something to play for each note when tuning his         guitar for his band.  I managed to re-find the demo on an old work         disk, and thus was able to extract the tune out.  I had sent him the         demo but only he and I probably ever had the release!" AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)

TITLE: Quadraped Tearaways
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "Originally, after the album music demo got rejected for Zzap! 64's         covermount tape, the plan was for this demo to be released in a         strictly limited edition of 100 copies. In the end I only distributed         20 of them. Eventually in 2017, 25 years after the demo was released,         I made it publicly available along with a PDF version of the novella I         wrote which I sent with the 20 disks.   And yes, the spelling of the         word quadruped is deliberately wrong in the album title - this was to         derail the trainspotters in the same style that Factory Records used to         do for those attempting to collect all their releases." STILENTRY: TITLE: Sensoria [from Micro-Phonies] ARTIST: Cabaret VoltaireCOMMENT: Based more on the 12" single version, which appears as a bonus         track on the CD version of the album.         "I've always been a big fan of Cabaret Voltaire, and the 12" version         of Sensoria is right up there with my favourites. I'd tried to do         a version of it back in 2009, but didn't get beyond the first 30         seconds or so. It was good to go back and start from scratch, and         concentrate first on getting the basslines right, and from there         build the tune up. It also plays a little bit faster than the         original does to keep it faster paced too. Naturally the bass         sounds massively better on a 6581 for which the tune was designed,         on an 8580 it just doesn't work so well." (WP)

TITLE: The Usurped Lord Leaps
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was my entry for the Transmission64 music competition. I wanted         to do something different, in terms of using a flute instrument as         the main lead, and build around that, with verse, chorus and middle         sections to set it all off.  It did work as I intended, and there's         also a hidden meaning to the title - the initials of the title spell         out TULL, a nod to Jethro Tull and particularly Ian Anderson, who is         the vocalist and flute player." (WP)

TITLE: Vehicular Hell
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "A little protest song I wrote about people who use the car for         every little journey, even when it's unnecessary, and how those         of us who are environmentally friendly have to suffer breathing         their car fumes. When we're all complaining about global warming         in the future, I just hope they can live with what they've done.         In the meantime, I'll stick to public transport." (WP)

TITLE: Arsenal
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was a work in progress of the title tune for the Arsenal FC         game licence which never was released. I wanted to use a football         type handclap chant as the main drum, and then throughout the title         tune it was going to reference some football songs with the drum         backing. The disk was thought to be lost when I moved house many         years ago, but found an unlabelled disk, and saw the file names on         there. When I loaded them into Ubik's Musik it was indeed this,         so pretty good to salvage it all round.         On the same disk as the Arsenal title tune, I'd put together a few         sound effects which could have played when you were playing the game         of football. I was also considering some football chants such as         those I'd used in the Football Tunes demo as well." (WP)

TITLE: Quadraped Tearaways (beta)
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: COMMENT: "This was the first known version of the demo.  It was Action Replay         frozen and sent off to Zzap! 64 for evaluation for their cover         mount cassette.  I had feed back from them a while later (they had         reformed as Commodore Force due to the financial collapse of the         publisher Newsfield) to ask if I could change the voices used on         the tunes, as they said it sounded the same.  In a way, it was a         good thing because I went back to the demo and spent some time         cleaning the music up and making it sound a whole lot nicer in         the end." TITLE: Yashar
AUTHOR: Warren Pilkington (Waz)
STILENTRY: TITLE: Yashar ARTIST: Cabaret VoltaireCOMMENT: "Based more on the John Robie 12" remix, which appeared as a 12" single         on the Factory Records label in 1982.  When Mute Records did a reissue         of the single "Nag Nag Nag" on CD in 1990, I bought it and it had both         the Robie remixes of Yashar on.  I used that CD as inspiration for doing         the cover version, and it was only years later I picked up the original         12" single and played that a fair bit too." (WP)

TITLE: Zarjaz 3.1

I thought I had         lost this, but turned out it was on an Action Replay saved version of         the editor I had.  I fixed it up to loop properly for release." (WP)
